title: The Weil representation and theta lifts
summary: Results classed as known in the literature and missing from Mathlib, proved here with their own definitions.

modules.title: Tame local characters, integral frames and the local Gauss sum
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.note:
`F` is a ring satisfying `New.SemilocalField`, modelled on a finite product of non-archimedean local
fields. Its integers are `O`, of volume one, and `ϖ` is a uniformiser. `New.invOnUnits χ` is `χ⁻¹`
on the units of `O` and zero elsewhere. `New.TameLocalChar χ` says that on `O`, `New.invOnUnits χ`
is a primitive character `η` of a finite ring `R` composed with a surjection `π` from `O` onto `R`
with kernel `ϖ O`. The file proves basic facts on such characters, introduces integral frames, and
shows that the Fourier transform of `New.invOnUnits χ` over `O` is γ·χ(ϖ t) when ϖ t is an integral
unit and zero otherwise, for some constant γ with ‖γ‖² = 1 / card R.

The quadratic Gauss sum that gives the product rule of the Weil representation at the finite places
is a different one; it is in `Lib.Weil.Construction.FiniteCocycle`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Exchange.IntegralFrame`: an integral basis in three blocks of columns `K, I, L` with its dual
  basis; `New.Exchange.IntegralFrame.blockRelations` lists the relations between the blocks.
* `New.Exchange.exists_local_gauss_sum`: the Fourier transform of the inverse of a tamely ramified
  character χ, cut off to the units, equal to γ·χ(ϖ t) when ϖ t is an integral unit and zero
  otherwise, for some γ with ‖γ‖² = 1 / card R.
* `New.Exchange.IntegralFrame.stdDatum`: the function x ↦ G(x (K I)) on integral matrices x, zero
  elsewhere.

Notions from other files:
* `New.SemilocalField`: Conditions met by a finite product of non-archimedean local fields: a
  locally compact ring with Haar measure, compact open subring O of volume one, a topologically
  nilpotent invertible ϖ in O, and `New.IsValuationPair O`.
* `New.HasIntegralConductor`: The additive character ψ is continuous and has conductor O: ψ is
  trivial on tO exactly when t lies in O.
* `New.IsIntegralUnit` x: x lies in O and has an inverse in O. `New.IsIntMatrix` O M: every entry of
  the matrix M lies in O.
modules.literature:
Known result: Gauss sums of a character of the determinant over matrix rings. Only one-dimensional
ramified characters are treated, and the exact value is not computed. For matrices over a finite
ring, the eigen-relation, the vanishing at singular index and the modulus are proved in another file
(`New.Exchange.exists_matrixFourier_eq_mul_inv_det`, used here). This file proves the scalar case
over the integers of a product of local fields, with the modulus. Source: T. Kondo, On Gaussian sums
attached to the general linear groups over finite fields, J. Math. Soc. Japan 15 (1963) 244–255; for
the scalar case over finite rings, E. Lamprecht, Math. Nachr. 9 (1953), see K. Conrad, Gauss and
Jacobi sums on finite fields and Z/mZ, §4; for the local scalar case, Tate's thesis §2.5.

See also `Lib.Weil.MixedModel.ZeroTerm`.

modules.title: Theta lifts of forms: products of minors, edges, arrows between spaces of forms
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.note:
This file studies theta lifts between spaces of automorphic forms on unitary groups. Over the reals,
`Ω` assigns operators on a Fock space to the points of a pair of real unitary groups, and `e`, `e'`
are kernels on the two groups; the forms of parameter `l` are those of type `New.typeKernel l s`. A
half edge relates `e` to `e'` through a Fock vector `Φ` and its lifts; an edge does so in both
directions. Edges together with finite data give arrows, data for which the global lift sends forms
to forms. The lift is equivariant under the finite points. The transposed lift is the lift for the
swapped kernel, and the descent `y' ↦ conj (transposed lift of conj y')` is the adjoint of the lift.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.isJointHighest_prod_det_pow_staircaseWeight`: a product of powers of nested minors, one nest
  for each sign, is nonzero, harmonic for both groups, and a highest weight vector for the rows and
  for the columns.
* `New.ParamsCorrespond`, `New.jointHarmonic`: parameters `l`, `l'` that correspond at every
  infinite place, and a chosen product of joint harmonics (`New.IsJointHarmonic`) for them.
* `New.IsHalfEdge`, `New.IsEdge`: `e` is a cusp kernel, and the integral of `⟨Φ, Ω (x, 1) Φ⟩`
  against `conj e` is not zero. The lift with `Φ` of a form of type `e` is a form of type `e'` once
  it has a level. The lift with each polynomial Fock vector is a real convolution of it. An edge has
  this both ways.
* `New.ParamsCorrespond.isEdge_jointHarmonic`: for corresponding parameters the chosen product is
  an edge for the real Weil representation.
* `New.formLift`, `New.IsArrow`: the lift on forms, and the data φ for which it sends forms of type
  e to forms of type e'.
* `New.IsEdge.isArrow`, `New.IsEdge.isForm_star_lift_swap`: an edge tensored with any finite datum
  gives arrows in both directions, and the descent sends forms of type e' to forms of type e.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`, `New.Space.lift`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in
  GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx equal to diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places; the theta
  lift h ↦ ∫_{[S]} θ(ω(g, h)φ) y(g) dg of y with datum φ.
* `New.Space.IsForm`, `New.typeKernel`: a form of type e is a bounded automorphic function that
  right convolution (`New.realConv`) with e fixes; `typeKernel l s` is the product over the infinite
  places of the kernels `dsKernel` with parameters l.
* `New.Fock.fockSpace`, `New.Fock.polyVector`, `New.Fock.piTensor`: the Fock space on ℂ^ι with its
  L¹ norm, the vector (polynomial times Gaussian) of a polynomial, and the product of Fock vectors
  in separate variables.
* `New.integratedRep`: for a representation π of U(diag ε) by bounded operators and a function f,
  the operator π(f) with π(f)x = ∫ f(g)π(g)x dg, when such a bounded operator exists.
modules.literature:
Known result: Joint harmonics and global theta lifts between discrete series types. Here the
parameter has large gaps, and the types are given by integrable projector kernels. The lift is shown
to carry forms fixed by one kernel to forms fixed by the other, in both directions, without Howe
duality. Source: J.-S. Li, Theta lifting for unitary representations with nonzero cohomology, Duke
Math. J. 61 (1990); Howe, JAMS 2 (1989); A. Ichino, arXiv 2002.09148, Lemma 7.8.

modules.title: Theta lifts for families of characters over a real edge and the seesaw of periods
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.note:
This file constructs theta lifts between two unitary groups for a whole family of characters at
once. For hermitian spaces `S`, `T` and characters `a`, `b` of the norm-one adeles,
`New.pairWeil S T a b` is the Weil representation of the pair. `New.modDatum` is a datum given by a
Fock vector at infinity and a function modulo `𝔪`, and a "type" is a kernel on the real points that
cuts out a space of forms.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Exchange.modLift`, `New.Exchange.modTransposedLift`: the lift of forms from `S` to `T` and
  the transposed lift back.
* `New.Exchange.IsConjKernelPair`, `New.Exchange.IsEdgeFamily`: a pair of conjugate cuspidal types;
  a family of characters with common weights for which two such pairs and a polynomial form a real
  edge (`New.IsEdge`). `New.Exchange.isEdgeFamily_of_paramsCorrespond` produces edges from
  corresponding parameters.
* `New.Exchange.pairLift`, `New.Exchange.pairTransposedLift`, `New.Exchange.IsPairEdge`: lift,
  transposed lift and edge when the two characters of the pair are given separately. `IsPairEdge`
  has one type on each group and lets the two characters have different tame parts.
* `New.Exchange.IsEdgeFamily.exists_lift_eq_realConv`,
  `New.Exchange.IsEdgeFamily.petersson_lift_eq_mul_inner_modTransposedLift`: replacing the
  polynomial of the edge by another one changes the lift by right convolution with a continuous
  compactly supported function on the real points; the Petersson product of a form with this lift is
  a constant times that of its transposed lift. The function and the constant do not depend on the
  finite data.
* `New.Space.periodPairing`: the bilinear period `∫ M z * f z * y (j z * r)` of a form `f` on `S`
  and a form `y` on `T`, for a moderate weight with function `M` and map `j` and a real point `r`.
* `New.Exchange.seesaw_periods`: suppose the theta kernels of two pairs agree up to moderate weights
  on a spanning set of polynomials (`New.Exchange.IsSeesawMatched`). Then proportionality to a fixed
  vector passes from the periods of lifts (`New.Exchange.modLift`) to the periods of transposed
  lifts (`New.Exchange.modTransposedLift`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to diag(s) at the infinite places (s the signs) and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.IsEdge`: a relation between kernels e, e' on the two real groups and a Fock vector Φ. The
  kernel e is a cusp kernel and the doubling zeta integral of Φ against ē is not zero. For a form of
  type e, the lift with Φ is a form of type e' if it has a level, and for a polynomial v the lift
  with v is the convolution of the lift with Φ by some α ∈ C_c. The same holds with the groups
  exchanged and the kernels ē', ē.
* `New.IsArrow`: the datum φ is an arrow e → e' for the theta kernel K if forms of type e on S are
  rapid and their lifts by φ are forms of type e' on T.
* `New.Space.Form`: `S.Form e` is the space of bounded automorphic functions on the group of `S`
  that right convolution with `e` fixes (when `e` is integrable).
* `New.modKernel`: the theta kernel of the datum `New.modDatum` made of the Fock vector of a
  polynomial and a function on matrices modulo `𝔪`. Along an edge the lift and the transposed lift
  integrate a form against this kernel, in the first and in the second variable.
modules.literature:
Known result: Seesaw identity for periods of theta lifts. Here the statement holds for two unitary
pairs whose kernels agree up to moderate factors for a spanning set of Fock polynomials. Both pairs
carry edge families (`IsEdgeFamily`), and the data are taken modulo an ideal. If finite sums of
periods of the lift are proportional to a fixed family of numbers at all real translates, then so
are those of the transposed lift. Source: S. Kudla, Seesaw dual reductive pairs, in Automorphic
forms of several variables (Katata 1983), Progr. Math. 46, Birkhäuser 1984, 244–268.

See also `Lib.Weil.Lift`.

modules.title: The jet matrix of a definite pair is a kernel for algebraic forms
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Theta lifts between definite unitary groups
modules.note:
An abstract theta kernel is an action of `G × G'` on a space of data, with a jet matrix for each
datum that is equivariant for the rational points. Such a kernel lifts algebraic forms from rank `n`
to rank `n'`.

* `New.IsLiftWeight`: the condition on ranks and weights under which the lift exists.
* `New.Kernel`: the abstract theta kernel.
* `New.Kernel.lift`, `New.Kernel.lift_equivariant`: the theta lift of a kernel and its equivariance
  under `G × G'`.
* `New.schurCoeffPoly`: the polynomial `Aᵀ S(z) ξ`, with `S = schur κ`.
  `New.dotProduct_schurJet_mulVec` writes the entries of the jet matrix as jets along it.
  `New.realPairWeil_schurCoeffPoly` gives the action of the real points on it, and
  `New.theta_pairWeil_schurCoeffPoly` its theta function as a coefficient of the jet matrix.
* `New.thetaKernel`: the kernel of the definite pair, which sends `f` to
  `schurJet κ (jetSeries _ c f)`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.𝒮`: The Banach space 𝒮(V) of integrable functions c on 𝔸^n with c(x) = ∫ c(y)β(y,x)e(x−y) dy,
  under the L¹ norm; β is the adelic bicharacter and e the vacuum function `New.vacuumFn`.
* `New.Space.finitePart`: The finite part 𝒮_f: the subspace of 𝒮(V) spanned by the translates of the
  vacuum under the finite Heisenberg operators `New.Space.finHeisenbergOp`.
* `New.rightStabilizer`: The subgroup of k in G with f(gk) = f(g) for all g.
* `New.AlgForm`: Smooth algebraic forms of weight (κ, e): functions φ on G_f with values in vectors
  indexed by `New.WeylIndex n κ`, with φ(γg) = ρ(γ)φ(g) for rational γ and an open stabiliser.
* `New.schurJet`: The matrix of jets of a power series along the entries of `schur κ`.

modules.title: Theta lifts between definite unitary groups and algebraic lifts by jets
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Theta lifts between definite unitary groups
modules.note:
This file studies the theta correspondence from the definite space `I_n` to `I_n'` (`New.stdSpace`),
for a weight that goes up from rank `n` to the larger rank `n'` (`New.IsLiftWeight`). There are two
lifts between these groups. The theta lift is an integral of a theta kernel over `[U(n)]`, and the
algebraic lift is a class sum with the matrix of jets `New.thetaKernel`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsHCParam.paramsCorrespond_iff`: the parameter `l` of the weight in rank `n` corresponds to
  `l'` (`New.ParamsCorrespond`) exactly when `l'` is the parameter of the weight `(κ, ea)` in rank
  `n'`, with the same columns `κ`.
* `New.exists_lift_ofAlgForm_eq_smul`: the analytic theta lift `New.Space.lift` with the joint
  harmonic `New.jointHarmonic` as real datum is a constant (possibly zero), divided by the index of
  the level, times the lift `New.Kernel.lift` of algebraic forms by `New.thetaKernel`.
* `New.isThetaLift_thetaKernel`: the lifts of the kernels of jets are theta lifts in the sense of
  `New.Space.IsThetaLift`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsLiftWeight`: `n < n'`, no column of `κ` has height strictly between the two ranks, and the
  exponent in rank `n` is `eb` plus the number `κ w (card n)` of columns of height `n`.
* `New.thetaKernel`: the kernel whose matrix at a finite datum is made of the Taylor coefficients
  (jets) of its theta series, paired with Schur polynomials.
* `New.IsHCParam`: `l` lists twice the Harish-Chandra parameter of the weight `(κ, e)`, in some
  order: at each place `w` the numbers `l w i` are distinct, and each of them is
  `hcParameter κ e (card n) w p` for some position `p < card n`.
* `New.stdSpace`: the definite space `I_n`, the sum of `n` norms with its standard lattice.
modules.literature:
Known result: Theta lift for a definite unitary pair as a class sum on algebraic modular forms. The
pair is U(n)×U(n′) over a CM field with `New.WeilData`, n < n′, and the kernel is the matrix of
Taylor coefficients of the theta function against Schur polynomials. The constant is left
unspecified. Source: B. Gross, Algebraic modular forms, Israel J. Math. 113 (1999); Kashiwara–Vergne
1978; R. Howe, Transcending classical invariant theory, JAMS 2 (1989).

modules.title: Heisenberg cocycles, vacua, the reproducing model and Schur's lemma
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Construction of the adelic Weil representation
modules.note:
This file sets up an abstract setting for the Weil representation that covers the real places
and the adeles. The data are a topological abelian group `W` with a measure `μ`, a Heisenberg
cocycle `β` on `W`, and a vacuum `e` for it. It also defines multiplier actions of a group `G` on
`W`. The vacuum defines a space of integrable functions reproduced by a kernel, on which `W` acts
by a Heisenberg representation `ρ`. The file proves superposition and Schur's lemma for this model.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Heisenberg W`: a continuous alternating bicharacter `β`, the cocycle of a Heisenberg group.
* `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum`: a function `e` on `W` that plays the part of the matrix coefficient of
  a vacuum vector (a Gaussian, or a lattice indicator times a semicharacter).
* `New.Heisenberg.MultiplierAction`: a group `G` acting on `W` by symmetries, with a multiplier `Δ`
  that turns a double integral of `e` and `β` attached to the action into a given `c` (by default
  `1`).
* `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.Model`: integrable v with v x = ∫ v y β(y, x) e(x - y), a Banach space
  for the L¹ norm, with the representation `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.heisenbergRep`, the vector
  `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.vacElem` and the form `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.modelInner`.
* `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.form_eq_mul_modelInner`,
  `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.eq_smul_one_of_commute`: Schur's lemma. An invariant form is a multiple
  of the inner product, and a bounded operator that commutes with the representation is a scalar.
  `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.integral_form_eq_mul_modelInner` treats a form given as an integral.

modules.title: Weil operators, orthogonal sums and transport of the reproducing model
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Construction of the adelic Weil representation
modules.note:
This file defines the Weil operators of a multiplier action of a group `G` on `W` on the
reproducing model of a vacuum. It proves their cocycle relation, and shows that they preserve the
inner product. For cocycle `1` it defines the Weil representation and proves that it intertwines
the Heisenberg operators and is continuous. The file then treats orthogonal sums `W = W₁ × W₂`,
with tensor products of model vectors and Wiener's bound, and the transport of the model along
isomorphisms.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.weilOp_mul`, `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.modelInner_weilOp`: if c(g, 1) = 1,
  the Weil operators `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.weilOp` multiply up to the cocycle c and preserve the
  inner product.
* `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.weilRep`: for c = 1 the Weil representation; it intertwines ρ(x) and
  ρ(gx) (`New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.weilRep_heisenbergOp`) and, for first countable G, is jointly
  continuous (`New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.continuous_weilRep`). Elements that preserve `e` act by Δ(g)
  times substitution (`New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.weilRep_apply_of_vacuum_smul`). The operator of g
  has norm at most ‖vac‖ |Δ(g)| (`New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.norm_weilRep_le`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.Model`: the integrable functions v with v x = ∫ v y β(y, x) e(x - y),
  with the L¹ norm and the inner product `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.modelInner`.
* `New.Heisenberg.MultiplierAction`: an action of `G` on `W` preserving `β` and `μ`, with a
  multiplier `Δ` and a cocycle `c`.
* `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.heisenbergOp`, `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.vacElem`: the Heisenberg
  operators ρ(x) on the model and the vacuum `e` as an element of the model.
modules.literature:
This file contributes to the adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta
functional. See `Lib.Weil.MixedModel.ZeroTerm`. Sources: Weil; Kudla.

The usual proof of the product rule ω(g) ω(h) = ω(gh) compares ω with a Schrödinger model on a
Siegel parabolic subgroup of a split space, and then uses the Iwasawa decomposition and the sum
V ⊕ V⁻. The proof here does not use a Schrödinger model. The scalar c(g, h) in
ω(g) ω(h) = c(g, h) ω(gh) is an integral of three vacua times values of the multiplier
(`New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.weilOp_inv_mul_weilOp_mul_weilOp`). Later files show directly that it is
1, from three local facts: a Gaussian determinant at the real places (`New.Fock.realAction`),
positivity at the split places and the sign of a Gauss sum at the inert places
(`New.stdLattice.mem_cocycleRadical`). The formulas of the Schrödinger model are then proved for the
slices in `Lib.Weil.MixedModel.ZeroTerm`.

modules.title: Splitting characters, Weil data, and the adelic Heisenberg cocycle and vacuum
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Construction of the adelic Weil representation
modules.note:
On a CM field `E` with CM type `Φ` (`New.CMType`; `Φ w` is the embedding τ : E → ℂ chosen at the
infinite place w), this file fixes the arithmetic data that determine the Weil representation. From
these data the file builds the adelic Heisenberg bicharacter and the vacuum function on `𝔸^n`, the
two ingredients of the adelic Weil representation.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.SplittingChar`: a splitting character `υ`, a unitary Hecke character with prescribed values
  on ideles whose finite part is a unit.
* `New.WeilData`: `υ` together with a purely imaginary `ȷ ∈ E`, which turns the hermitian form into
  a Heisenberg cocycle, and a finite idele `α`, which scales the vacuum lattice.
* `New.WeilData.scaleIdele`: the idele with finite part `α` that normalises the real coordinates.
* `New.adelicHeisenberg`: the bicharacter β(x, y) = ψ(½ȷ y*Sx), where S is `New.stdForm`, the
  diagonal form with signs `s` at the infinite places and 1 at the finite ones.
* `New.vacuumFn`: the vacuum, a Gaussian at the infinite places times a function of modulus one on
  the lattice αÔ^n of finite vectors (zero off the lattice). It does not depend on `s`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.𝔸`: The ring ℂ^f × 𝔸_f, one copy of ℂ for each infinite place of E times the finite adeles:
  the adele ring of E when E is totally complex.
* `New.ψf`: The standard additive character of the finite adeles: ψ_f(x) = exp(2πi Tr_{E/ℚ}(a)) for
  any a in E with x − a integral.
* `New.Heisenberg`: A continuous function β on W × W, W a topological abelian group, with values of
  modulus one, multiplicative in each variable, and β(x,x) = 1.

modules.title: Finite Heisenberg datum, its lattice vacuum and the finite multiplier
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Construction of the adelic Weil representation
modules.note:
This file treats the finite part of the standard Heisenberg model on vectors `ι → 𝔸f E` of finite
adeles of a CM field `E`. The elements `j`, `α` and the character `υ` come from `New.WeilData`, and
`New.ψf` is the standard character. We write `Ô` for `New.Ô E`, `ψ₀` for the complex character
`New.stdLattice.selfDualAddChar E`, z ↦ `ψf (j α ᾱ z)`, `x* y` for `star x ⬝ᵥ y`, and `c₀` for the
integral element `WeilData.traceOne` of `E`, which satisfies `c₀ + star c₀ = 1`. This file builds
the finite Heisenberg datum and its vacuum on the standard lattice. It defines the finite multiplier
`Δ_f` through saturating matrices and proves its laws on the finite unitary group `New.Gf`. It also
proves a lemma that fixes a sign by a congruence modulo `4`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.stdLattice.isVacuum_finVac`: `New.stdLattice.finVac` is a vacuum (`New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum`)
  for `New.stdLattice.finHeisenberg`. The convolution identity follows from
  `New.stdLattice.finVac_add` and the self-duality of the lattice.
* `New.glMultiplier`, `New.glMultiplier_mul_diagGL_mul`: the multiplier on `GL_ι(𝔸_f)` and its value
  in terms of elementary divisors, from which its laws are read off.
* `New.finMultiplier`: its restriction to the finite unitary group `New.Gf`, with
  `New.finMultiplier_inv`, `New.norm_finMultiplier_sq`, `New.upsilon_mul_finMultiplier` and
  `New.finMultiplier_eq_of_supportedOn`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.WeilData`: Weil data on a CM field E with a primitive 5040th root of unity, so that E/E⁺ is
  unramified at the finite places. They consist of ȷ in E with ȷ = −ȷ̄, Im τȷ > 0 for every τ in the
  CM type and (1 − ȷ⁻¹)/2 integral; a finite idele α for which the completed integers Ô are
  self-dual under (z, u) ↦ ψ_f(ȷαᾱzu); and a splitting character υ equal to −1 at uniformisers of
  the places w with w = w̄.
* `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum`: a vacuum for β and μ is a continuous, integrable, even, real function e
  with e(0) = 1 and ∫ e(z)e(x−y−z)β(z,y)β(z+y,x) dμ(z) = e(y)e(x).

modules.title: The finite cocycle as a finite Gauss sum, and its triviality
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Construction of the adelic Weil representation
modules.note:
This file treats the matrix action of the finite unitary group `New.Gf` on the finite Heisenberg
datum `New.stdLattice.finHeisenberg` of vectors `ι → 𝔸f E`, with vacuum `New.stdLattice.finVac` and
multiplier `New.finMultiplier`. We write `Ô` for `New.Ô E`, `ψ₀` for
`New.stdLattice.selfDualAddChar E`, `x* y` for `star x ⬝ᵥ y`, and `c₀` for `WeilData.traceOne`.
The double integral in the resulting cocycle is a finite Gauss sum, and the cocycle equals `1`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.stdLattice.exists_gauss_sum_finProjAction`: the double integral in the cocycle is a Gauss sum
  over a finite module over `New.Ô`, the ring of integral finite adeles.
* `New.stdLattice.mem_cocycleRadical`: the cocycle is `1` at all `g` and `s`.
* `New.finAction`: the same action with cocycle `1`, as used for the adelic Weil representation.

Notions from other files:
* `New.WeilData`: Weil data on a CM field E: ȷ in E with ȷ = −ȷ̄, a finite idele α for which Ô is
  self-dual under (z, u) ↦ ψ_f(ȷαᾱzu), and a splitting character υ.
* `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum`: a vacuum for β and μ is a continuous, integrable, even, real function e
  with e(0) = 1 and ∫ e(z)e(x−y−z)β(z,y)β(z+y,x) dμ(z) = e(y)e(x).
* `New.Heisenberg.MultiplierAction`: an action of G on W that preserves β and μ. It comes with a
  continuous multiplier Δ: G → ℂ such that Δ(1) = 1, Δ(g⁻¹) = conj Δ(g) and Δ(g)Δ(h)Δ((gh)⁻¹) ∬
  e(hx)e(ghy)β(x,y)e(x+y) = c(g,h).

modules.title: The adelic Weil representation on 𝒮(V) and its theta functional
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Construction of the adelic Weil representation
modules.note:
The adelic Heisenberg datum β = `New.adelicHeisenberg E s` on `𝔸 ^ n`, with vacuum function e =
`New.vacuumFn`, splits into a real and a finite part. The data of the adelic Weil representation
(measure, multiplier Δ and action of the adelic unitary group `New.G E s`) are built as products of
the real and the finite data. For a hermitian space with a point `V` (`New.Space`), the space
`New.𝒮 V`, whose vectors are also called data, is the model `Model (adelicHeisenberg E s)`. It
carries the Heisenberg operators `New.Space.ϱ` (`ρ x` or `heisenbergOp x` on the model), the Weil
representation `New.Space.ω`, the inner product `New.Space.dataInner` (`⟨·, ·⟩`, conjugate linear on
the left) and the vacuum `New.Space.vacElem`. A theta functional is a bounded functional on the
model that is invariant under the rational vectors `New.Space.ratVectors` and normalised;
`New.Space.θ` is a definite choice of one. A vector `f : 𝒮 V` applied to `x` is its theta function
θ(ϱ(x) f), not the integrable function `f.1 x = ⟨ϱ(x) vac, f⟩`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.adelicSum`: multiplication by the idele `New.WeilData.scaleIdele` identifies complex
  coordinates, indexed by pairs (infinite place, index), times finite adelic vectors with `𝔸 ^ n`.
  The bicharacter and `New.vacuumFn` become products of those of `New.Fock.realHeisenberg` and
  `New.stdLattice.finHeisenberg` (`New.Heisenberg.OrthogonalSum`). This scaling turns the adelic
  Gaussian into the standard one (`New.WeilData.conj_scaleIdele_mul`).
* `New.adelicAction`: the adelic unitary group `New.G` acts on `𝔸 ^ n` by matrices, keeping the
  bicharacter and the measure, and `Δ` satisfies the identity of `New.Heisenberg.MultiplierAction`
  with trivial cocycle.
* `New.Space.omega_rho`, `New.Space.dataInner_omega`, `New.Space.dataInner_vacElem_omega_vacElem`:
  `ω g` takes `ϱ x` to `ϱ (g x)`, keeps the inner product, and has overlap `(conj (Δ g))⁻¹` with the
  vacuum.
* `New.Space.exists_isThetaFunctional`, `New.Space.IsThetaFunctional.eq_smul`: a theta functional
  exists, and every invariant functional is a multiple of it.
* `New.Space.dataInner_eq_quotMean`, `New.Space.hasSum_dataInner`: the inner product as a mean of
  theta functions, and the product of two theta values as a sum of inner products.

Notions from other files:
* `New.adelicHeisenberg`: the Heisenberg datum on adelic n-space with bicharacter β(x,y)=ψ(½ȷ
  h(y,x)), h being the standard hermitian form of signs s and ȷ = −ȷ̄ the element `j` of the Weil
  data.
* `New.Heisenberg.OrthogonalSum`: an isomorphism W₁ × W₂ ≃ W along which the bicharacter and the
  vacuum function of W are the products of those of W₁ and W₂.
* `New.Heisenberg.MultiplierAction`: an action of a group on W that keeps β and the measure, with a
  multiplier Δ that satisfies the cocycle identity of the Weil representation.
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places; `New.Space.vecAtPoint` sends
  y in E^n to the adelic vector x⁻¹y.
* `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.Model`: the space of integrable v with v(x) = ∫ v(y) β(y,x) e(x−y) dμ(y),
  as a type.

modules.title: Vacuum projections and the finite part of the Weil representation
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Construction of the adelic Weil representation
modules.note:
This file studies the projection P^S = `New.Space.projOn` S on the vectors that are vacua above a
set S of finite places. It shows that P^S is a self-adjoint projection and relates it to the
Heisenberg operators and to the Weil representation. It defines the finite part
`New.Space.finitePart` and shows that this subspace is stable under ϱ_f, under the projections and
under the finite unitary group. It also shows that the translates of the vacuum by representatives
modulo Ô^n form an orthonormal spanning family of the finite part.

The Weil representation ω of the adelic unitary group acts on 𝒮(V) = `New.𝒮`, together with the
Heisenberg operators ϱ(y) = `New.Space.ϱ` y. The operators of finite vectors,
ϱ_f = `New.Space.finHeisenbergOp`, are normalised to represent Ô^n = `New.stdLattice`:
ϱ_f(y) = `semichar` y • ϱ(`finVec` y), where finVec y has real part 0 and finite part αy (α the
finite idele of the Weil data) and `semichar` y is a root of unity, and vac = `New.Space.vacElem` is
the vacuum; ψ₀ = `selfDualAddChar E` is a character of 𝔸f E trivial on Ô, `half` is ½, and
`traceOneAdele` t satisfies t + t̄ = 1. For a set S of finite places of E, P^S = `New.Space.projOn`
S is the mean of ϱ_f(`idem` T • y) over y ∈ Ô^n, where `idem` T is the finite adele equal to 1 above
T and 0 elsewhere, for T = S ∪ S̄ = `Set.conjClosure` S; it projects onto the vectors that are vacua
above S. The finite part `New.Space.finitePart` is the span of the ϱ_f-translates of vac.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.omega_projOn`, `New.Space.projOn_omega`: ω(g) commutes with P^S if g is integral on S;
  P^S ω(g) is a scalar on the image of P^S if g is supported above S.
* The finite part is stable under ϱ_f, under the projections `New.Space.projOn` and under the finite
  unitary group (`New.Space.omega_mem_finitePart`). The real vacuum projection `New.Space.projReal`
  fixes it.
* `New.Space.dataInner_finHeisenbergOp_rep_vacElem`, `New.Space.span_finHeisenbergOp_rep_vacElem`:
  the translates of vac by representatives of the classes modulo Ô^n are orthonormal and span the
  finite part.
* `New.Space.exists_eq_smul_omega_vacElem`: a vector of the finite part fixed by the lattice `g Ô^n`
  is a multiple of `ω(g) vacElem`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to the diagonal matrix of its signs at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.𝒮`: The Banach space 𝒮(V) of integrable functions c on 𝔸^n with c(x) = ∫ c(y)β(y,x)e(x−y) dy,
  under the L¹ norm; β is the adelic bicharacter and e the vacuum function `New.vacuumFn`.
* `New.Space.vacElem`: The vacuum: the function e (Gaussian times twisted lattice indicator) as an
  element of 𝒮(V).

This file forms the product f₁ ⊠ f₂ = `New.Space.boxProd` of data along a splitting of the
coordinates that is compatible with the signs. It also defines the block diagonal embedding
`New.G.blockEmb` of the two unitary groups. It shows that the product is compatible with the
Heisenberg operators, the vacua, the inner products, the insertion of real Fock vectors and the
Weil representation of block diagonal elements. It defines the changes of coordinates
`New.CoordChange` that keep the vacuum, and the transport `New.CoordChange.map` of data along them.
It shows that the transport preserves norms and respects the Heisenberg operators, the vacuum,
the insertion of a real vector, and the Weil representation up to a scalar.

modules.title: Jet series of theta functions and translation by rational vectors
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Construction of the adelic Weil representation
modules.note:
Let V be a hermitian space with a point over a CM field E, with data space 𝒮(V). Let `α` be
the finite idele of the Weil data, let `finVec x` be the adelic vector `(0, α x)`, let
`finiteImage γ` be `α⁻¹ γ` in `(𝔸f E)ⁿ` (finite adeles) for γ in Eⁿ, so that
`finVec (finiteImage γ)` is `(0, γ)`, and let `V.ϱ (finVec x)` be translation along a finite vector
`x`. The file turns theta functions into Taylor series and Schur jet matrices, and defines when the
jets of two data are conjugate. For a standard space V it shows that translation by the finite image
of a rational vector acts on theta functions as the opposite real translation.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.jetSeries`: the series of the theta values of `f` along the monomials; for standard `V`
  and `f` in the finite part it is the Taylor series of the theta function of `f`, scaled by `a`.
* `New.schurJet`: the matrix of jets of a power series along the entries of the Schur matrix.
* `New.Space.IsJetConjugate`: the jets of `f'` are the `σ`-conjugates of the jets of `f`, up to a
  permutation of the infinite places.
* `New.entireTheta_translate_finiteImage`: for standard `V`, `New.Space.entireTheta` turns
  translation by `finiteImage γ` into the twisted translation by `-realImage γ`.
* `New.semichar_finiteImage`: the semicharacter at the finite image of a rational vector is the
  inverse of the canonical multiplier at minus its real image.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to the diagonal matrix of its signs at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.Space.θ`, `New.Space.integrated`: The theta functional on the space `New.𝒮 V` of data, and
  the datum v ⊗ f for v in the Fock space and f in `New.𝒮 V`.
* `New.WeilData`: supplies the purely imaginary `j` (ȷ) in E, the finite idele `α` and the integer
  `traceOne` (c₀) with c₀ + c̄₀ = 1.
* `New.Space.entireTheta` sends `f` to `y ↦ f(y) exp(|y|²/2)` on real points; `New.Space.ϱ` is
  Heisenberg translation; `New.Space.finitePart` is the span of the finite translates of the vacuum.

modules.title: The dictionary between vectors and theta functions
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Construction of the adelic Weil representation
modules.note:
For rational vectors `γ` in `Eⁿ`, with real images in `ℂ^(Φ × n)`, this file defines the Riemann
form, the translations `T_γ` of functions on `ℂ^(Φ × n)` and the theta functions for a lattice.

* `New.ratShift_ratShift`, `New.mem_star_smul_idealLattice_iff`, `New.signedShift_add`: the law of
  composition of the translations `T_γ`, the duality of `δ̄ 𝔞₀ⁿ` and `δ⁻¹ 𝔞₀ⁿ` for the Riemann form,
  and the signs that make the translations a homomorphism on `𝔞₀ⁿ`.
* `New.Space.entireTheta_rho`: for a standard space, the Heisenberg translation `V.ϱ (finVec x)`,
  with `x = α⁻¹ γ` the finite image of a rational vector `γ`, acts on theta functions as `T_(-γ)`.
* `New.Space.range_apply_finVec_eq_range_ratShift_entireTheta`: for a standard space and `φ` in the
  finite part, the values of `φ` at the finite adelic vectors are the values
  `T_γ (entireTheta φ) 0`.
* `New.Space.isThetaFunction_iff`: for a standard space, the theta functions for `𝔞₀ⁿ` are the
  multiples of the theta function of the vacuum, because the Riemann form on `𝔞₀ⁿ` is unimodular.

Here `ℂ^(Φ × n)` stands for `InfinitePlace E × n → ℂ`, and `Φ w` is the embedding of `E` in `ℂ` that
the CM type chooses at the infinite place `w`.

Notions from other files:
* `realImage γ`: the entry at `(w, i)` is `Φ w (γ i)` divided by the `w`-part of the idele
  `scaleIdele E`; `finiteImage γ` is `α⁻¹ γ` in `(𝔸f E)ⁿ`, with `α` the finite part of this idele.
* `stdLattice E n`: the lattice `Ôⁿ` of integral finite adelic vectors; it is its own dual for the
  character `selfDualAddChar E`.
* `semichar x`: the value `selfDualAddChar E (traceOneAdele * half * star x ⬝ᵥ x)`, where
  `traceOneAdele` is the image of `traceOne = c₀ : E`, with `c₀ + c̄₀ = 1`.
* `𝒮 V` is the space of vectors of the Weil representation of a space `V`, with vacuum `V.vacElem`
  and Heisenberg action `V.ϱ`; `entireTheta φ` is the theta function of `φ`.
* `V.IsStd`: all signs of `V` are `+1` and its point is the identity matrix.

modules.title: Fourier inversion for theta functions
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Construction of the adelic Weil representation
modules.note:
Let `δ` be integral with `δ δ̄` a nonzero natural number and let `r` be the number of elements of
`InfinitePlace E × n`, that is, the number of infinite places times the rank.

* `New.Space.exists_entireTheta_eq_of_isThetaFunction`: a theta function for `δ̄ 𝔞₀ⁿ` is the theta
  function of a vector `φ` of the finite part `V.finitePart` (a subspace containing the vacuum and
  stable under the translations `V.ϱ (finVec _)`).
* `New.Space.fourier_inversion`: if the theta function of `φ` is one for `δ̄ 𝔞₀ⁿ` and `y` runs over
  `δ⁻¹ 𝔞₀ⁿ⧸𝔞₀ⁿ`, the signed sums of translates of `ρ(-y) φ` over `𝔞₀ⁿ⧸δ̄ 𝔞₀ⁿ` are multiples
  `c_y vac` of the vacuum, and `∑ c_y ρ(y) vac = (δ δ̄) ^ r φ`, with `ρ` the finite translation.
* `New.Space.norm_mul_vacElem_le_one_of_eq_sum`: if the values of `φ` at the vectors `finVec x` are
  integral at a prime, then so are those of such a multiple `c_y vac`.

Here `φ` lies in `𝒮 V`. In the first two results the space `V` is standard (`V.IsStd`: all signs are
`+1` and the point is the identity); the third holds for every space. The theta functions of these
sums are theta functions for `𝔞₀ⁿ`, and orthogonality of the characters of `δ⁻¹ 𝔞₀ⁿ⧸𝔞₀ⁿ` inverts the
summation.

Notions from other files:
* `idealLattice E n` is the lattice `𝔞₀ⁿ` in `Eⁿ` of the vectors with integral finite image
  `finiteImage`, and `Ô E` is the ring of integral finite adeles.
* `ratShift γ` is the translation `T_γ` of functions on `ℂ^(InfinitePlace E × n)`, `ratPhase γ γ'`
  the commutator of `T_γ` and `T_γ'`, and `signedShift γ` the translation `T_γ` times the
  semicharacter at `γ`.
* `IsThetaFunction Y F` says that `F` is entire and fixed by the signed translations along `Y`.
* `entireTheta φ` is the theta function of a vector `φ` of `𝒮 V`. The vector `V.vacElem` is the
  vacuum, `V.ϱ` the translation by adelic vectors and `V.finHeisenbergOp` the signed finite
  translation.

principal polarization. The proof is by Fourier inversion on a finite abelian group. Source:
Mumford, Tata lectures on theta I.

modules.note:
For hermitian spaces `S`, `T` (`New.Space`) of ranks `n`, `n'`, the `n' × n` matrices form a space
`Hom(S, T)`. The pair `(g, h)` acts on it by `x ↦ h x g⁻¹`. The Weil representation `New.Space.ω` of
that space restricts to the pair. Theta kernels are also built from a polynomial at the real places
and a function modulo an ideal at the finite places.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.hom`, `New.G.onHom`: the space `Hom(S, T)` and the map `U(S) × U(T) → U(Hom(S, T))`.
* `New.pairWeil S T a b`: the representation of the pair, twisted by `a (det h) * b (det g)⁻¹`
  (`New.pairChar`), for characters `a, b` of `[U(1)]` (`New.AutChar`).
* `New.pairTheta`: the theta kernel, the theta functional `New.Space.θ` of
  `pairWeil S T a b (g, h) f`.
* `New.Modulus`: a non-zero ideal `𝔪` of `𝓞 E` such that no prime `w` divides it together with the
  complex conjugate of `w`; `New.Modulus.ResidueRing` is the finite ring `𝓞 E ⧸ 𝔪`,
  `New.Modulus.places` the set of primes dividing `𝔪` and `New.Modulus.reduction` a reduction map
  from `New.Ô E`.
* `New.modDatum`: the vector in the data space of `New.Space.hom S T` with real part `v`, with `Ψ`
  at the primes dividing `𝔪` (`New.Space.schrodingerOp`) and the vacuum elsewhere.
* `New.modKernel`: its theta kernel `New.pairTheta`, for `v` the Fock vector of a polynomial;
  `New.stdKernel`: this kernel for the standard characters `New.stdChar` of `S` and `T`.

* `New.Space`: a hermitian space over a CM field E with `CMType E` (a chosen embedding at each

modules.title: Short isotropic vectors and means of theta functionals over isotropic subspaces
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Dual pairs of unitary groups and their theta kernels
modules.note:
This file prepares the rapid decay of theta kernels under a support condition on Ψ, on the data
space of Hom(S, T), which carries the representation `New.pairWeil`. The datum v ⊗ Ψ ⊗ f₀ is
`integrated _ v (schrodingerOp _ P Ψ f₀)`, with v in Fock space, Ψ Schwartz–Bruhat above a set P
of finite places disjoint from its conjugate (`New.IsSchwartzBruhat`), and f₀ in the finite part
`New.Space.finitePart`. The argument is the one for cusp forms. At a point of large height the
lattice has a short isotropic vector, and θ is invariant under the rational maps of rank one
through it. The mean over the adelic maps of this kind vanishes by the support condition on Ψ
(`New.map_schrodingerOp_eq_zero_of_invariant`), and θ is close to this mean because the maps are
short (`New.Space.exists_norm_sub_subspaceMean_le`).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.exists_short_isotropic`: If the height of `g` exceeds `2`, then the lattice of `S` at
  `g` contains a nonzero isotropic vector, written as a matrix with one column, of length at most
  `2 / height g` (`latticeBall`).
* `New.Space.exists_norm_sub_subspaceMean_le`: for vectors `z i` of the lattice at `g` of lengths
  at most `δ` spanning an isotropic subspace `Z`, a bounded functional invariant under the
  Heisenberg operators of `Z` is close, on data with finite part `f₀`, to its mean
  `New.Space.subspaceMean` over the adelic points of `Z` modulo the rational ones.

Notions from other files:
* `New.G`: The adelic unitary group G = G_∞ × G_f for signs s at the infinite places and the
  identity matrix at the finite places.
