modules.title: Laws of the Weil action of a pair: translations, real points, levels, rational maps
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Dual pairs of unitary groups and their theta kernels
modules.note:
Let `S`, `T` be hermitian spaces (`New.Space`). A pair `p = (g, h)` of adelic points of their
unitary groups acts on `Hom(S, T)` by `x ↦ h x g⁻¹` (`New.G.onHom`). It acts on the Weil
representation of `Hom(S, T)` by `New.pairWeil S T a b p`, the Weil operator times
`New.pairChar a b p = a (det h) / b (det g)`. The file proves that this action preserves the inner
product. It also describes the action of the real points `(x, y)` of the two unitary groups of signs
`s`, `s'` on the Fock space. It then writes maps, the Heisenberg cocycle and the Heisenberg
operators of `Hom(V, V')` in rational coordinates and defines theta lifts.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.pairWeil_of_mem_Gamma`: rational points (`New.Space.Γ`) act by `f ↦ f (h⁻¹ · g)`.
* `New.pairTheta_mul`, `New.continuous_pairTheta`: the theta kernel `New.pairTheta` satisfies
  `pairTheta S T a b f (p * q) = pairTheta S T a b (pairWeil S T a b q f) p`, and it is continuous.
* `New.realPairWeil γ γ'`: the representation on the Fock space `New.PairFock E s s'` of
  `Hom(S, T)`. It is the oscillator operator of `z ↦ y z x⁻¹` times `det y ^ γ * det x ^ (-γ')` at
  each place.
* `New.pairWeil_integrated`, `New.pairWeil_integrated_all`: on `New.Space.integrated _ v f`, the
  vector `f` with its real vacuum replaced by `v`, real points act on `v` by `New.realPairWeil` and
  finite points act on `f`.
* `New.exists_level_pairWeil`: a datum in the finite part `New.Space.finitePart` of `Hom(S, T)` (the
  span of finite Heisenberg translates of the vacuum) is fixed under `New.pairWeil` by a product of
  open subgroups of the two finite adelic unitary groups.
* `New.Space.IsThetaLift`: a family of maps between spaces of forms computes the theta integrals
  between standard positive spaces.

Notions from other files:
* `New.G`: The adelic unitary group G = G_∞ × G_f for signs s at the infinite places and the
  identity matrix at the finite places.
* `New.GInf E s`: the real points, one complex unitary group `U(diag s)` for each infinite place;
  `New.homSigns s s'` is the sign vector `(i, j) ↦ s' i * s j` of `Hom(S, T)`, and `New.realSigns`
  repeats a sign vector at every infinite place.
* `New.Fock.realWeil`: The Weil representation of U(ε) on the Fock space `𝓕 ε`; its multiplier
  `New.Fock.realMultiplier u` is the conjugate of the determinant of the negative block of u.
* `New.blockDiagAlg ε`: the complex matrices that commute with `diag ε`, that is, the block
  diagonal matrices for the partition of the indices by sign; `New.principalMinor y p` is the
  determinant of the block of `y` on the indices that satisfy `p`.
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places; `New.Space.Γ` is the group
  of rational points of its unitary group, inside `New.G`.
* `New.AutChar E`: the continuous characters of the norm-one adeles `U(1)(𝔸)` that are trivial on
  rational points; `a`, `b` are such characters.
* `New.Space.hom`: The space `Hom(S, T)` of `n' × n` matrices, indexed by pairs (row, column);
  `New.matrixToVec` reads a matrix as a vector on these pairs.

modules.title: Weil representation of unitary pairs: finite action, sums, negation and change of point
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Dual pairs of unitary groups and their theta kernels
modules.note:
This file studies the Weil representation `New.pairWeil` S T a b of a pair of unitary groups on
data on Hom(S,T). Here S and T are hermitian spaces of ranks n and n′, Hom(S,T) is the space of
n′ × n matrices, and θ denotes the theta functional. The file describes the action of finite points
on named data. It also describes the behaviour of the action and of θ when a space is split as a
sum, when the form of one space is negated, and when a point is moved.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.pairWeil_schrodingerOp_of_mem_supportedOn`: a pair supported on `A` and its conjugate
  (`New.Gf.supportedOn`) replaces `Ψ` by `Ψ (h⁻¹ · g)`, up to an explicit scalar.
* `New.pairWeil_schrodingerOp_of_mem`: an integral pair (`New.stdLevel`) moves `Ψ` and the vector
  together.
* `New.conj_weilMultiplier_of_eq_neg`, `New.exists_theta_negSource`: negation conjugates the
  multiplier and θ, up to a factor; `New.pairWeil_negSource`: it intertwines the actions of the pair
  once the characters are changed.

Notions from other files:
* `New.pairWeil`: The representation ω_{a,b}(g, h) = a(det h) b(det g)⁻¹ ω(`onHom` (g, h)); the
  scalar is `New.pairChar a b (g, h)`.
* `New.weilMultiplier`: Δ(g) = Δ_f(g_f) ∏_τ conj(det d_τ), with d_τ the block of g_τ on the negative
  coordinates.
* `New.Space.boxProd`: the product f₁ ⊠ f₂ of data on two blocks of coordinates.
* `New.Space.ϱ`, `New.Space.ω`, `New.Space.vacElem`: The Heisenberg operators, the Weil
  representation and the vacuum vector of the space of data `New.𝒮 V`.

modules.title: Mixed models and zero terms of a pair with one split space: Levi and radical laws
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Dual pairs of unitary groups and their theta kernels
modules.note:
Let V = range l ⊕ ιV₀ ⊕ range k be a splitting of a hermitian space V over V₀
(`New.Space.Splitting`: isotropic dual frames k, l and an isometry ι, the field `i`, from V₀), and
let T be another space. The splitting induces splittings of Hom(V,T) and Hom(T,V). This file
computes, for these, the zero term and the mixed model of the representation `New.pairWeil` of the
pair.

* `New.Space.Splitting.homSource`, `New.Space.Splitting.homTarget`: the induced splittings of
  Hom(V,T) over Hom(V₀,T) and of Hom(T,V) over Hom(T,V₀).
* `New.Space.Splitting.homSlice`: the term f[x] of an adelic n' × p matrix x in the mixed model;
  `New.Space.Splitting.hasSum_theta_homSlice`: θ(f) is the sum of the θ(f[T.x⁻¹x]) over rational
  x; `New.Space.Splitting.symm_homSource_zeroTerm_eq_integral`: the integral of the terms over
  adelic x is the zero term for the splitting with k and l exchanged;
  `New.Space.Splitting.homSlice_rho`: the law of f[x] under the Heisenberg operators.
* `New.Space.Splitting.homSource_zeroTerm_pairWeil`,
  `New.Space.Splitting.homTarget_zeroTerm_pairWeil`: the zero term of ω(g,h)f, resp. ω(h,g)f, when
  gk = km.
* `New.Space.Splitting.homSlice_levi`, `New.Space.Splitting.homSlice_radicalElement`: the laws of
  f[x] under the Levi subgroup and under the radical of the stabiliser of range k.

Notions from other files:
* `New.pairWeil V T a b (g, h)`, written ω_{a,b}(g,h): the Weil representation of x ↦ h x g⁻¹ on the
  data of Hom(V,T), twisted by a(det h) b(det g)⁻¹.
* `New.Space.ϱ`: the Heisenberg operators on the data space 𝒮 of a space.
* `New.Space.Splitting.zeroTerm` (ev): the mean of f(ιy + kb) over b in 𝔸^p / E^p;
  `New.Space.Splitting.slice x f` is ev(ϱ(lx) f).

`kAdelic`, `iAdelic` and `lAdelic` are the frames in adelic coordinates; `kCoord`, `iCoord` and
`lCoord` send kb + ιw + la to b, w and a. In formulas ȷ is `WeilData.j`, ψ is `stdAddChar`, υ is the
splitting character and * is the conjugate transpose.

modules.title: Growth of theta kernels and convergence of theta lifts
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Dual pairs of unitary groups and their theta kernels
modules.note:
This file proves growth estimates for theta kernels `(g, h) ↦ θ (ω (g, h) φ)` on the product of
the adelic groups of two spaces `S` and `T`, for a representation `ω`, a functional `θ` and a
vector `φ`. Using reduction theory, it first bounds the norm of `ω (g₀, γ g)`, for fixed `g₀` and
a suitable rational translate `γ g`, by a power of the height `New.Space.height` of `g`. The lift
`New.Space.lift` of a function `y` integrates the kernel against `y g` over `[S] = Γ_S \ G_S`.
For `y` of rapid decay the lift converges, the lifts from `S` and from `T` are transposes of each
other, and the adjoint of the lift for the Petersson products is the descent.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.ThetaKernel.moderate_growth`: the kernel grows at most like a power of the heights
  `New.Space.height`.
* `New.ThetaKernel.integrable_theta_mul`, `New.ThetaKernel.liftBilin`,
  `New.ThetaKernel.exists_clm_lift`: for `y` of rapid decay (`New.Space.rapidFunctions`) the lift
  converges, is bilinear in `φ` and `y`, and is continuous in `φ`.
* `New.ThetaKernel.integral_mul_lift_eq_integral_mul_lift_swap`,
  `New.ThetaKernel.petersson_lift_eq_petersson_descent`: the lifts from `S` and from `T` are
  transposes of each other, and the descent is the adjoint of the lift.

Notions from other files:
* `New.G`: The adelic unitary group G = G_∞ × G_f for signs s at the infinite places and the
  identity matrix at the finite places.
* `New.Space`: A hermitian space with a point: a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx equal to
  diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places; Γ = x⁻¹U(J)(E)x.
* `New.Space.IsAutomorphic`, `New.Space.IsRapid`: a function F is automorphic if it is continuous,
  left Γ-invariant and right invariant under an open subgroup of G_f; it is rapid if |F(g)|·ht(g)^B
  is bounded for every B, and moderate (`New.Space.IsModerate`) if |F(g)| ≤ C·ht(g)^A for some C and
  A.

modules.title: Semilinear maps intertwining the Weil action up to σΔ/Δ
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Dual pairs of unitary groups and their theta kernels
modules.note:
This file gives an abstract form of the Galois law for the Weil representation. A map `L` on the
data `𝒮 V` that is semilinear along `σ : ℂ →+* ℂ` may keep the finite part and turn the finite
Heisenberg translation by `x` into that by `b x`, where `σ` takes `ψ z` to `ψ (b b̄ z)` for the
additive character `ψ = New.stdLattice.selfDualAddChar E` of the finite adeles. Such a map also
intertwines the Weil action, on the finite part and for finite points, up to the factor σ(Δ_f)/Δ_f,
with Δ_f the finite multiplier `New.finMultiplier`. Writing `b = u a` with `u` unitary and `a` a
unit of `Ô`, the laws are first proved for `ω(u)⁻¹ L`, which scales translations by `a`. Finite
vectors are read through `finVec x = (0, α x)`, with `α` the idele of the Weil data.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.ScalesTranslations`: the property of a `σ`-semilinear map to keep the finite part and
  to turn the finite translation by `x` into that by `b x`, while `σ` takes `selfDualAddChar E z` to
  `selfDualAddChar E (b b̄ z)`; `New.Space.ScalesTranslations.map_omega` is its law for `ω`, and
  `New.Space.ScalesTranslations.exists_map_schrodingerOp` its law for the vacuum and for the vectors
  `V.schrodingerOp R Ψ V.vacElem` with `Ψ` Schwartz–Bruhat at a set `R` of finite places.
* `New.multiplierRatio`: The factor `σ (Δ g) / Δ g`, for the multiplier `Δ = New.finMultiplier` of a
  finite unitary point `g`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space.ϱ`, `New.Space.ω`, `New.Space.vacElem`: The Heisenberg operators, the Weil
  representation and the vacuum vector of the space of data `New.𝒮 V`.
* `New.scalarFin` (`Lib.Weil.DualPair.FiniteAction`): the scalar matrices, as a homomorphism from
  the finite adeles of norm one to `Gf E n`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Galois action on CM theta functions and on the finite Weil representation. Here it is
stated for semilinear maps on the finite part of the data that scale the Heisenberg translations,
with an explicit factor; such a map is built from Taylor series of theta functions in
`New.UpperBound.Kernels.JetConjugatesAndBounds`. Source: G. Shimura, Theta functions with complex
multiplication, Duke Math. J. 43 (1976) 673-696; for the rationality of the Weil representation, J.
Trias, On the rationality of the Weil representation and the local theta correspondence, arXiv
2601.16141.

modules.title: Rapid decay of theta kernels of unitary dual pairs under support conditions
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Dual pairs of unitary groups and their theta kernels
modules.note:
This file proves that the theta kernel `New.pairTheta` of the dual pair U(S) × U(T), acting on
data on Hom(S, T) through `New.pairWeil`, decays rapidly under support conditions on the finite
datum `Ψ`. The kernel is `(g, h) ↦ θ (ω (g, h) φ)`, with `g` in the adelic group of `S` and `h` in
that of `T`. At a point of large height the proof uses short pairs of rational matrices
(`New.IsShortPair`) and the rational maps of rank one `dᵢ ⟨cⱼ, ·⟩` that they span.
`New.modDatum S T 𝔪 Ψ v` is the datum `v ⊗ Ψ ⊗ vac` on `Hom(S, T)`, where `Ψ` is a function on
matrices modulo an ideal `𝔪` prime to its conjugate (`New.Modulus`), and `New.pairTheta` is its
theta kernel on `U(S) × U(T)`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.pairTheta_decay_of_onto`: rapid decay of the theta kernel on U(T) when Ψ is supported on
  surjective maps.
* `New.pairTheta_decay_of_injective`: rapid decay of the theta kernel on U(S) when Ψ is supported on
  injective maps.
* `New.pairTheta_modDatum_decay`: suppose some place divides `𝔪` and `Ψ` is supported on left
  invertible matrices. Then the kernel decays rapidly in the height of `g`, with polynomial growth
  in the height of `h`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: A hermitian space with a point: a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx equal to
  diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places; Γ = x⁻¹U(J)(E)x.
* `New.Space.IsAutomorphic`, `New.Space.IsRapid`: a function F is automorphic if it is continuous,
  left Γ-invariant and right invariant under an open subgroup of G_f; it is rapid if |F(g)|·ht(g)^B
  is bounded for every B, and moderate (`New.Space.IsModerate`) if |F(g)| ≤ C·ht(g)^A for some C and
  A.
* `New.Modulus.liftFn`: A function Ψ of vectors modulo 𝔪 read on finite adelic vectors x: Ψ of the
  reduction of the components of x at the places dividing 𝔪 if these are integral, else 0.
* `New.Space.coordMatrix` (in `Lib.Weil.DualPair.ShortIsotropicVectors`): the coordinates
  `g⁻¹ x⁻¹ c` at an adelic point `g` of a matrix `c` over `E`.
* `New.Space.adelicPoints` (in `Lib.Weil.DualPair.ShortIsotropicVectors`): the span over the
  adeles of the adelic vectors of the elements of a subspace `Z` of `V`.
modules.literature:
Theta kernels of unitary dual pairs, with functoriality, seesaw, growth and rapid decay, are known.
Here both spaces are hermitian and act on the maps between them. Decay is proved for data
supported on maps of full rank at split places, using small shifts along a short isotropic vector
instead of Siegel sets. Source: S. Kudla, Seesaw dual reductive pairs, Progr. Math. 46 (1984);
Harris, Kudla, Sweet, Theta dichotomy for unitary groups, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 9 (1996), section 1;
for decay, Kudla, Rallis, A regularized Siegel-Weil formula: the first term identity, Ann. Math. 140
(1994).

modules.title: Theta kernels of unitary pairs modulo an ideal: formal laws and seesaw identities
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Dual pairs of unitary groups and their theta kernels
modules.note:
This file proves the formal laws of the theta kernel θ^{S,T}_{a,b}[Ψ,P](g,h) =
`New.modKernel` S T a b 𝔪 Ψ P g h. Here S and T are spaces of ranks n and n′, and a and b are
characters of [U(1)]. Ψ is a function on n′ × n matrices over O_E/𝔪, and P is a polynomial whose
variables are indexed by an infinite place and a matrix position (row, column). The kernel is
`New.pairTheta` of the datum `New.modDatum`; the laws cover bilinearity, twisting, integral
translations, seesaw identities, negation, passing to a smaller ideal and relabelling.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_conj_modKernel_eq_mul_modKernel_neg`, `New.exists_stdKernel_neg_left`: the complex
  conjugate of a kernel is a kernel for the negated first space, up to a factor of modulus one.
* `New.modKernel_mul_stdLevel_left`, `New.modKernel_mul_stdLevel_right`: right translation by the
  lattice stabiliser `New.stdLevel` acts on Ψ through its reduction `New.Modulus.reductionGL`, up to
  a scalar; `New.modDatum_factor`, `New.modKernel_factor`: passing to a smaller ideal.
* `New.modKernel_block_right`, `New.modKernel_sum_right`, `New.modKernel_sum_left`,
  `New.Rows.modKernelStdSpace_block`: seesaw identities, the kernel of a direct sum at block
  diagonal elements is a product; `New.stdKernel_sum_right`, `New.stdKernel_sum_left`: the same with
  standard characters; `New.stdKernel` S T 𝔪 is `New.modKernel` S T (stdChar s) (stdChar s') 𝔪, with
  s, s′ the signs of S, T.

Notions from other files:
* `New.pairWeil`: The representation ω_{a,b}(g, h) = a(det h) b(det g)⁻¹ ω(`onHom` (g, h)); the
  scalar is `New.pairChar a b (g, h)`.
* `New.Modulus`: a nonzero ideal of O_E prime to its complex conjugate, that is, never divisible by
  both w and w̄; `𝔪.ResidueRing` is O_E/𝔪 and `𝔪.places` the set of primes dividing 𝔪.
* `New.Space.boxProd`: the product f₁ ⊠ f₂ of data on two blocks of coordinates.
* `New.negSource` (`Lib.Weil.DualPair.FiniteAction`): the change of coordinates x ↦ (1, u⁻¹) x from
  Hom(S⁻,T) to Hom(S,T); `negSource.map` pulls data on Hom(S,T) back to data on Hom(S⁻,T).
modules.literature:
Known; see `Lib.Weil.DualPair.GaloisLaw` for sources.

See also `Lib.Weil.DualPair.ThetaLiftConvergence`.

modules.title: Flipping a dual pair by adjoints: Weil actions and theta kernels modulo ideals
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Dual pairs of unitary groups and their theta kernels
modules.note:
For hermitian spaces `V`, `W`, the Weil representation on the data space of `Hom(V, W)` gives the
action `New.pairWeil V W` of the two unitary groups and the theta kernel `New.pairTheta V W`.
Taking adjoints identifies this pair with the pair `(W, V⁻)`, where `V⁻ = New.Seesaw.flipSpace V`
has the signs opposite to those of `V`. This file gives the effect of the adjoint on Weil actions,
on theta kernels and on the polynomial vectors of the Fock model (`New.flipPoly`). For theta
kernels `New.modKernel` built from functions on matrices modulo an ideal `𝔪`, the flip is expressed
by a finite Fourier transform.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.flipCoords`: the adjoint, twisted by the idele `New.flipIdele`, as a change of coordinates
  `New.CoordChange`; it depends on a unit `c` of `Ô` with `c̄ c = -1`. `New.Seesaw.flipSpace` is the
  opposite space `V⁻`.
* `New.flipCoords_map_pairWeil`, `New.exists_theta_flipCoords_map_eq_mul`,
  `New.flipCoords_map_schrodingerOp`: it intertwines the actions of the pairs once the characters
  are changed, keeps the theta functional up to a number of modulus one, and moves a datum to the
  conjugate places.
* `New.exists_pairTheta_flip`: the resulting identity of theta kernels, after a change of point.
* `New.Modulus.exists_modKernel_flip`: a kernel `New.modKernel` of (V, S) as a constant times a
  kernel of (S, T), where V has the signs opposite to T.
* `New.Exchange.exists_conj_modKernel_eq_swap`: the complex conjugate of a kernel of (S, T) as a
  kernel of (T, S).

Notions from other files:
* `New.WeilData`: Weil data on a stably unramified E. They consist of ȷ in E with ȷ = −ȷ̄, Im τȷ > 0
  for every τ in the CM type and (1 − ȷ⁻¹)/2 integral; a finite idele α for which the completed
  integers Ô are self-dual under (z, u) ↦ ψ_f(ȷαᾱzu); and a splitting character υ equal to −1 at
  uniformisers of the places w with w = w̄; its restriction to the norm-one ideles is
  `New.WeilData.upsilonU1`.
* `New.Modulus`: a nonzero ideal 𝔪 of O_E prime to its complex conjugate; `𝔪.ResidueRing` is O_E/𝔪,
  `𝔪.generator` a finite idele generating 𝔪 in Ô, equal to 1 off 𝔪, and `𝔪.primAddChar` the
  primitive additive character x ↦ ψ_f(ȷαᾱ x / 𝔪.generator) of O_E/𝔪.
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to the diagonal matrix of its signs at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.𝒮`: The Banach space 𝒮(V) of integrable functions c on 𝔸^n with c(x) = ∫ c(y)β(y,x)e(x−y) dy,
  under the L¹ norm; β is the adelic bicharacter and e the vacuum function `New.vacuumFn`.
* `New.pairWeil`: The action ω_{a,b}(g, h) = χ_{a,b}(g, h) ω(x ↦ hxg⁻¹) on 𝒮(Hom(S, T)), where
  χ_{a,b}(g, h) = a(det h) b(det g)⁻¹ is `New.pairChar`. The theta kernel `New.pairTheta` S T a b f
  (g, h) is θ(ω_{a,b}(g, h) f), where θ is the theta functional `New.Space.θ`.

modules.title: Terms of theta kernels at rational matrices and basic laws of theta integrals
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Dual pairs of unitary groups and their theta kernels
modules.note:
This file studies the theta kernel `New.pairTheta S T α β f` of a pair of hermitian spaces (S, T)
and the theta integral `New.Exchange.thetaIntegral S T α β f`, which is its integral over `[U(T)]`.
When S is split along an isotropic subspace (`New.Space.Splitting`), the terms of the kernel at
rational matrices are invariant under (x, h) ↦ (γ x, γ h) for rational γ in U(T). Some results
concern data with real part a Fock vector `v`, finite part `y ↦ φ (π y)` at the places `A` (where
`π` reads the components at `A`), and the vacuum elsewhere. For such data the file describes how the
two unitary groups act.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.Splitting.exists_tsum_thetaTerm_le`: the terms are absolutely summable, with moderate
  growth in h.
* `New.Space.Splitting.exists_tsum_thetaTerm_schrodingerOp_le`: under a support condition on Ψ the
  sum of their absolute values is bounded in h.
* `New.Space.Splitting.hasIntegrableTerms_integrated_schrodingerOp`: so this sum is integrable over
  the adelic quotient of U(T) (`New.Space.Splitting.HasIntegrableTerms`).
* `New.Exchange.ReadsAt.pairWeil_localDatum_of_mem_stdLevel`, `New.Exchange.thetaIntegral_pairWeil`:
  how the two unitary groups act.
* `New.Exchange.IsTargetBounded`: a growth bound on the kernel, under which the integral is linear
  in the datum (`New.Exchange.exists_linear_thetaIntegral`) and automorphic
  (`New.Exchange.IsTargetBounded.isAutFunction_thetaIntegral`).
* `New.Exchange.ReadsAt.isTargetBounded`: the bound holds when `F ≠ 0`, `v` has all moments finite
  and `φ` is locally constant of compact support and vanishes off the right invertible matrices.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to the diagonal matrix of its signs at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.𝒮`: The Banach space 𝒮(V) of integrable functions c on 𝔸^n with c(x) = ∫ c(y)β(y,x)e(x−y) dy,
  under the L¹ norm; β is the adelic bicharacter and e the vacuum function `New.vacuumFn`.
* `New.pairWeil`: The action ω_{a,b}(g, h) = a(det h) b(det g)⁻¹ ω(x ↦ hxg⁻¹) on 𝒮(Hom(S, T)).
* `New.Space.integrated`, `New.Space.schrodingerOp`: The operators f ↦ v ⊗ f for a Fock vector v and
  f ↦ Ψ ⊗ f for a function Ψ on finite adelic vectors.

modules.title: Holomorphic data, functions of a level, and theta kernels modulo 𝔪 as level multipliers
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Dual pairs of unitary groups and their theta kernels
modules.note:
This file sets up vocabulary for holomorphic automorphic functions on a unitary group over the CM
field E. It covers holomorphic data in the Fock space, adelic holomorphy, rapidly decreasing
functions of a given level, and additive characters of matrices modulo 𝔪. It also proves that
multiplication by a theta kernel `New.modKernel` preserves level N. Here the kernel's finite datum
is a function on matrices modulo 𝔪, and 𝔪 is generated by N. This needs the character `b` to have a
tame part that is trivial off the places of 𝔪.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Rows.holomorphicData`: Fock vectors all of whose matrix coefficients on the first group are
  holomorphic of weight u. `New.Rows.prod_mem_holomorphicData` and
  `New.Rows.mem_holomorphicData_of_highestVector` give such vectors.
* `New.Rows.IsAdelicHol`: adelic functions holomorphic in the archimedean variable.
  `New.Rows.isAdelicHol_pairTheta` passes from a holomorphic vector to its theta kernel.
* `New.Rows.rapidOfLevel`: rapidly decreasing automorphic functions (members of `V.rapidFunctions`)
  of a given level. The set is closed under conjugation, and `New.Rows.mul_sum_mem_rapidOfLevel`
  treats products with linear combinations.
* `New.Rows.mul_modKernel_mem_rapidFunctions`, `New.Rows.mul_modKernel_mem_rapidOfLevel`:
  multiplying by the kernel in the first variable keeps rapid decay, and keeps the level `N` if `N`
  generates the modulus.

Notions from other files:
* `New.PairFock`: The Fock space for the signs s′_i s_j of the pair, at all infinite places.
* `New.Space`: A hermitian space over E; its automorphic functions live on the adelic group `New.G`,
  and `New.Space.IsRapid` is decay faster than every power of the height.
* `New.pairTheta`: The theta kernel θ(ω_{a,b}(g,h)f) of two hermitian spaces; `New.modKernel` is
  this kernel for the datum made of a function on matrices modulo 𝔪 and the Fock vector of a
  polynomial.
* `New.AutChar.HasWeight b e ψ`: The character b has weight e at the infinite places and tame part
  ψ, given by a character of each residue field.
modules.literature:
Known result: Harmonic highest vectors for (U(p,q), U(n)) give holomorphic vectors. Proves a special
case: highest vectors, such as products of leading minors, that are killed by each mixed
second derivative ∂²/∂x_{ca}∂x_{cb} with a, b of opposite signs have matrix coefficients that extend
holomorphically with an explicit weight. This hypothesis is stronger than pluriharmonic in the sense
of Kashiwara–Vergne, where only the sums over c must vanish. Source: M. Kashiwara, M. Vergne, On the
Segal–Shale–Weil representations and harmonic polynomials, Invent. Math. 44 (1978) 1–47, III 6.3,
7.2; M. G. Davidson, The harmonic representation of U(p,q) and its connection with the generalized
unit disk, Pacific J. Math. 129 (1987) 33–55.

See also `Lib.Weil.DualPair.ThetaLiftConvergence`.

modules.title: Two edges V → V′ → V″ joined into one datum of the pair (V′, V⁻ ⊕ V″)
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Dual pairs of unitary groups and their theta kernels
modules.note:
This file joins data on two consecutive edges V → V′ → V″ into one datum of the pair
(V′, V⁻ ⊕ V″), where V⁻ ⊕ V″ is `New.Seesaw.flipSum`. A datum on `Hom(V, V′)` is carried by the
adjoint to `Hom(V′, V⁻)` and multiplied with a datum on `Hom(V′, V″)`. The joining map is
compatible with the theta functional `New.Space.θ`, with translations and with the Weil actions,
which become `New.Seesaw.tripleWeil`. On the finite parts `New.Space.finitePart`, the spans of the
finite translates of the vacuum, it induces an injective map from the tensor product onto the
finite part.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Seesaw.arrowProduct`: for two consecutive edges V → V′ → V″, the bounded bilinear map that
  joins data on Hom(V, V′) and Hom(V′, V″) into one datum of the pair (V′, V⁻ ⊕ V″). It is
  compatible with the theta functional up to a nonzero constant (`New.Seesaw.theta_arrowProduct`)
  and with the Weil actions (`New.Seesaw.arrowProduct_twistedPairWeil`).
* `New.Seesaw.homHeisenbergOp_arrowProduct`, `New.Seesaw.finHeisenbergOp_arrowProduct`: the
  joining map is compatible with translations.
* `New.Seesaw.arrowTensor`: the induced map on the tensor product of the finite parts. It is
  injective (`New.Seesaw.injective_arrowTensor`), with a left inverse
  (`New.Seesaw.leftInverse_arrowTensor`), and its range is the finite part
  (`New.Seesaw.range_arrowTensor`).
* `New.Seesaw.theta_tripleWeil_rat_mul`: `θ` of `New.Seesaw.tripleWeil` is invariant under rational
  points in the first two groups.

Notions from other files:
* `New.WeilData`: Weil data on a stably unramified E. They consist of ȷ in E with ȷ = −ȷ̄, Im τȷ > 0
  for every τ in the CM type and (1 − ȷ⁻¹)/2 integral; a finite idele α for which the completed
  integers Ô are self-dual under (z, u) ↦ ψ_f(ȷαᾱzu); and a splitting character υ equal to −1 at
  uniformisers of the places w with w = w̄; its restriction to the norm-one ideles is
  `New.WeilData.upsilonU1`.
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to the diagonal matrix of its signs at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.𝒮`: The Banach space 𝒮(V) of integrable functions c on 𝔸^n with c(x) = ∫ c(y)β(y,x)e(x−y) dy,
  under the L¹ norm; β is the adelic bicharacter and e the vacuum function `New.vacuumFn`.
* `New.pairWeil`: The action ω_{a,b}(g, h) = χ_{a,b}(g, h) ω(x ↦ hxg⁻¹) on 𝒮(Hom(S, T)), where
  χ_{a,b}(g, h) = a(det h) b(det g)⁻¹ is `New.pairChar`. The theta kernel `New.pairTheta` S T a b f
  (g, h) is θ(ω_{a,b}(g, h) f), where θ is the theta functional `New.Space.θ`.
* `New.Seesaw.flipSpace` (in `Lib.Weil.DualPair.Flip`): the opposite space V⁻ of V, with matrix −J
  and the opposite signs.

modules.title: The Fock model of the Weil representation of U(ε) at a real place
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: The Fock model of the real Weil representation
modules.note:
For signs ε : ι → {±1}, this file builds the Fock model of the Weil representation of the unitary
group U(ε) = `New.USign` ε. The polynomial vectors v_P(x) = P(ζ(x)) exp(−|x|²/2), where ζ =
`New.Fock.holomorphicCoord` ε conjugates the positive coordinates, lie in the Fock space. Products
along splittings of the coordinates and over real places are compatible with polynomial vectors.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Fock.realMultiplier`, `New.Fock.norm_realMultiplier_le`: the multiplier of the Weil
  representation, the conjugate of the negative minor, is bounded by ‖u‖^{|ι|}.
* `New.Fock.realAction`: the unitary group `U(ε)` acts on the datum in the sense of
  `New.Heisenberg.MultiplierAction`, with multiplier `New.Fock.realMultiplier` (the conjugate
  determinant of the negative block) and cocycle `1`.
* `New.Fock.fockSpace`, `New.Fock.realWeil`, `New.Fock.realHeisenbergOp`, `New.Fock.vacVector`,
  `New.Fock.fockInner`: the space, the Weil representation of U(ε), the Heisenberg action, the
  vacuum, the inner product.
* `New.Fock.polyVector`: the vector v_P(x) = P(ζ(x)) exp(−|x|²/2) of a polynomial P. It lies in the
  Fock space because derivatives of the Heisenberg action on the vacuum produce all polynomials.
* `New.Fock.polyVector_injective`: P ↦ v_P is injective.
* `New.Fock.piTensor`: the product of a family indexed by `T` (the real places), a vector on
  `T × ι`; it is compatible with polynomials and inner products.
* `New.Fock.blockU`, `New.Fock.realWeil_piTensor`: block diagonal unitary matrices act factor by
  factor.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Heisenberg`: A continuous function β on W × W, W a topological abelian group, with values of
  modulus one, multiplicative in each variable, and β(x,x) = 1.
* `New.Fock.normalizedVolume`: Lebesgue measure on `ι → ℂ` divided by `π ^ card ι`.
* `New.principalMinor`: the determinant of the block of a square matrix on the indices that
  satisfy a condition.
* `New.Heisenberg.IsVacuum.modelSubmodule`: The complex subspace of integrable functions v on W
  satisfying the reproducing identity v(x) = ∫ v(y) β(y,x) e(x−y) dμ(y) for every x, where β is the
  bicharacter, e the vacuum and μ the measure.

modules.title: Moments on Fock space, approximation by polynomial vectors, bounds for functionals
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: The Fock model of the real Weil representation
modules.note:
The Fock space `New.Fock.fockSpace` consists of functions on ℂ^ι reproduced by the Gaussian. This
file defines weighted L¹ norms ∫ (1 + ‖y‖)^N |v y| dy on it, with values in [0, ∞], and proves
growth estimates that justify integrals and limits at the real places. Vectors whose moments are all
finite are approximated in all these norms by polynomial vectors. A functional controlled by its
differences under short Heisenberg translations is then bounded by moments.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Fock.fockMoment`: the weighted L¹ norm ∫ (1 + ‖y‖)^N |v y| dy, with values in [0, ∞];
  `New.Exchange.IsSchwartzVector`: all these norms are finite (a Schwartz vector).
* `New.Fock.fockMoment_realHeisenbergOp_le`, `New.Fock.fockMoment_realWeil_le`,
  `New.Fock.fockMoment_integral_le`: bounds under the Heisenberg translations
  `New.Fock.realHeisenbergOp`, the Weil representation `New.Fock.realWeil`, and integrals of
  vectors.
* `New.Fock.fockMoment_polyVector_ne_top`, `New.Fock.exists_tendsto_fockMoment`: the vectors
  polynomial times Gaussian (`New.Fock.polyVector`) have finite norms, and approximate in all norms
  at once every vector whose norms are finite.
* `New.Fock.exists_norm_realHeisenbergOp_polyVector_le`: for a functional ℓ controlled by its
  differences under translations of size at most t ≤ 1, the value at the translate by z of a
  polynomial vector is at most C ‖ℓ‖ tᴺ (1 + ‖z‖)ᴺ.
* `New.Fock.exists_enorm_le_mul_fockMoment_of_norm_sub_le`: the bound ‖ℓ v‖ ≤ C ‖ℓ‖ tᴺ times the
  N-th moment of v, for every vector v.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Fock.fockSpace`: the Fock space of integrable functions c on ℂ^ι with c(x) = ∫ c(y) β(y,x)
  e(x−y) dy, where e is the Gaussian exp(−|x|²/2), under the L¹ norm.
* `New.Fock.realHeisenberg`: For signs ε, the Heisenberg datum on ℂ^ι given by the continuous
  unit-modulus bicharacter β(x,y) = exp((y*εx − x*εy)/2) = exp(i Im y*εx).
* `New.Fock.realHeisenbergOp` y: the Heisenberg translation c ↦ (z ↦ β(y,z) c(z − y)) on the Fock
  space.
* `New.Fock.vacVector`: the Gaussian `New.Fock.realVac` as a vector of the Fock space.
* `New.Fock.holomorphicCoord` ε x: the holomorphic coordinates of x, x̄ᵢ where εᵢ = 1 and xᵢ
  otherwise.

modules.title: Polynomial vectors in Fock space: inner product, density and Weil derivative
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: The Fock model of the real Weil representation
modules.note:
The polynomial vectors v_P = `New.Fock.polyVector` ε P lie in the Fock space `New.Fock.fockSpace`
with signs ε. On this space U(ε) acts by the Weil representation ω₀ = `New.Fock.realWeil`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Fock.fockMatrixCoeff_raiseOp`, `New.Fock.fockMatrixCoeff_lowerOp`: how the operators
  `New.Fock.raiseOp`, `New.Fock.lowerOp` (multiplication by X_a or differentiation, according to
  the sign ε_a) move across ω₀(u) in a matrix coefficient `New.Fock.fockMatrixCoeff`.
* `New.Fock.fockInner_X_mul`, `New.Fock.fockInner_polyVector`: X_i is adjoint to ∂_i, so ⟨v_P, v_Q⟩
  is the Fischer pairing (P̄(∂)Q)(0). For monomials see `New.Fock.fockInner_polyVector_monomial`.
* `New.Fock.denseRange_polyVector`: the vectors v_P are dense.
* `New.Fock.hasDerivAt_realWeil`: along a curve in U(ε) through 1 with velocity Y, ω₀ has derivative
  v_Q on v_P, where Q = `New.Fock.weilDeriv` ε Y P.

The action of block diagonal isometries on the v_P by substitution is
`New.Fock.realWeil_polyVector_of_mem_blockDiagAlg` in `Lib.Weil.DualPair.WeilAction`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Fock.vacVector`: The Gaussian exp(−|x|²/2) regarded as an element of the Fock space.
* `New.USign`: For a vector of signs ε, the unitary group U(J) of the diagonal matrix J=diag(ε).

modules.title: Harmonic matrix coefficients of the Weil representation and oscillator pairs on matrices
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: The Fock model of the real Weil representation
modules.note:
Let ω₀ = `New.Fock.realWeil` be the Weil representation of U(ε) on the Fock space. Let u be block
diagonal with respect to labels d, and let P, Q be harmonic: ∂_i∂_j kills them whenever d_i = d_j
and ε_i ≠ ε_j. Then the coefficient ⟨v_Q, ω₀(u) v_P⟩ is an inner product after a linear
substitution, divided by the determinant of the negative block of u. The dual pair U(ε) × U(ε′) acts
on the Fock space of R × C matrices, and the pulled-back, det-twisted Weil representations of the
two factors form an oscillator pair.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Fock.complexLinearPart`: the matrix formed from the positive block of u and the conjugate of
  its negative block; it is invertible.
* `New.Fock.fockMatrixCoeff_eq_fockInner`: the coefficient is an inner product after a linear
  substitution (`New.linSubst`), divided by the determinant of the negative block of u.
* `New.Fock.detTwist`: the Weil representation `New.Fock.realWeil` pulled back along a homomorphism
  f and twisted by det^γ; `New.Fock.isUnitaryRep_detTwist`, `New.Fock.isDerivedAction_detTwist`,
  `New.Fock.fockInner_detTwist_pos` give unitarity with polynomial growth of the operator norm
  (`New.IsUnitaryRep`), the derivative (`New.IsDerivedAction`) and positivity at positive definite
  elements.
* `New.OscillatorRep`, `New.OscillatorPair`: these three properties as a structure, for U(ε) acting
  on the Fock space of an arbitrary dual-pair datum `T : New.FockDualPair ε ε' ι`, and for commuting
  actions of U(ε) and of U(ε′) (the latter via `T.swap`).
* `New.Fock.oscillatorPair_detTwist`: the twisted left and right actions on matrices form such a
  pair.

Notions from other files:
* `New.USign`: for a vector of signs ε, the unitary group U(ε) of the diagonal matrix diag(ε).
* `New.Fock.fockInner`: the bounded sesquilinear form (c, c′) ↦ ∫ c̄ c′ on the Fock space,
  conjugate-linear in the first variable.
* `New.Fock.polyVector`: the linear map P ↦ v_P from complex polynomials to the Fock space,
  v_P(x) = P(ζ(x))exp(−|x|²/2), where ζ(x)_i is x̄_i at positive and x_i at negative coordinates.
* `New.Fock.fockMatrixCoeff`: the coefficient ⟨v_Q, ω₀(u) v_P⟩, written `fockMatrixCoeff u Q P`.
* `New.Fock.weilDeriv`: the derivative of `New.Fock.realWeil` on polynomials, the linear map u ↦ Σ
  u_ab A_a B_b, where (A_a, B_a) is (X_a, ∂_a) if ε_a = 1 and (−∂_a, X_a) otherwise; A_a is
  `raiseOp ε a` and B_a is `lowerOp ε a`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Bargmann–Fock model of the harmonic (oscillator) representation of U(p,q). Here the
space is the L¹ (Feichtinger) space of vacuum coefficients rather than the Hilbert Fock space, and
weighted moments replace Schwartz seminorms. This file treats unitarity, growth, the derivative and
the coefficients between harmonic polynomials. Source: M. G. Davidson, The harmonic representation
of U(p,q) and its connection with the generalized unit disk, Pacific J. Math. 129 (1987), §1 and
Prop. 2.2; G. B. Folland, Harmonic Analysis in Phase Space (1989), ch. 1, 4; H. Reiter, Metaplectic
Groups and Segal Algebras, LNM 1382 (1989).

modules.title: Mixed Schrödinger–Fock models and rapid sections with prescribed values
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Mixed Schrödinger models, zero terms and named data
modules.note:
A mixed model reads a vector `Φ` of a large Fock space `New.Fock.fockSpace` as a function
`x ↦ h.slice x Φ` on `ℂ ^ p` with values in a smaller Fock space. An adapted splitting of a
hermitian space induces one at the infinite places (`New.Space.Splitting.IsAdapted.mixedModel`). A
vector is a Schwartz vector (`New.Exchange.IsSchwartzVector`) if all its moments `fockMoment N
v = ∫⁻ y, (1 + ‖y‖) ^ N * ‖v y‖ ∂normalizedVolume` are finite; `New.Fock.realWeil` is the Weil
representation.

The file shows that the values of a mixed model decay rapidly. It also constructs Schwartz vectors
with prescribed smooth compactly supported values, using Fourier inversion in `x` and non-stationary
phase.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Fock.MixedModel`: the structure, described by the action of the Heisenberg operators
  `New.Fock.realHeisenbergOp` and by the value of the vacuum.
* `New.Fock.MixedModel.exists_fockMoment_slice_le`: the values decay rapidly in `x`, in the moments
  `New.Fock.fockMoment`.
* `New.Fock.MixedModel.exists_isSchwartzVector_slice_eq`: if `τ` is smooth of compact support, `u`
  is a smooth unitary family and `ξ` is a Schwartz vector, then `x ↦ τ x • realWeil (u x) ξ` is
  `x ↦ h.slice x Φ` for a Schwartz vector `Φ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Fock.fockSpace`: the Fock space: integrable functions c on ℂ^ι with c(x) = ∫ c(y)β(y,x)e(x−y)
  dy, e the Gaussian exp(−|x|²/2), under the L¹ norm for the measure `New.Fock.normalizedVolume` on
  ℂ^ι.
* `New.Fock.vacVector`: the Gaussian exp(−|x|²/2) regarded as an element of the Fock space.
* `New.Fock.realHeisenberg`: for signs ε, the Heisenberg datum on ℂ^ι given by the continuous
  unit-modulus bicharacter β(x,y) = exp((y*εx − x*εy)/2) = exp(i Im y*εx), where ε stands for
  `signMatrix ε`, the diagonal matrix of the signs.

modules.title: Schwartz–Bruhat functions on a set of places and the Schrödinger model there
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Mixed Schrödinger models, zero terms and named data
modules.note:
Functions on finite adelic vectors that only see the components at a set `S` of finite places, and
the action of the Heisenberg group on them when `S` is disjoint from its conjugate.

* `New.IsSchwartzBruhat S Ψ`: `Ψ` is Schwartz–Bruhat above `S`. Examples are the indicator
  `New.boxIndicator` of the vectors integral on `S` and the coset functions `New.cosetIndicator`.
* `New.IsSchwartzBruhat.eq_sum_cosetIndicator`, `New.IsSchwartzBruhat.mem_of_cosets`: such a
  function is a finite linear combination of coset functions.
* `New.schrodingerAct`: the Schrödinger model, with the Heisenberg law
  `New.schrodingerAct_schrodingerAct`. `New.semichar_smul_schrodingerAct` gives its form in the
  normalisation that represents the lattice, and its vacuum is the box function
  (`New.schrodingerAct_boxIndicator`).
* `New.Space.mem_range_schrodingerCombination`: every Schwartz–Bruhat function above `S` is a finite
  combination of Heisenberg translates of the box function.

Notions from other files:
* `New.idem S`: the finite adele with component 1 at the places of `S` and 0 elsewhere, so that
  `idem S • x` is the part of `x` at `S`.
* `New.stdLattice.selfDualAddChar`: a character of the finite adeles for which `Ô^n` is its own dual
  under the pairing `selfDualAddChar E (y* x)`.
* `Set.conjClosure`: the set `S ∪ S̄` of the places in `S` and their complex conjugates;
  `Set.IsConjDisjoint S` says that `S` and `S̄` are disjoint.
* `New.stdLattice.half` is `1 / 2`, `New.stdLattice.traceOneAdele` an integer `c₀` with
  `c₀ + c̄₀ = 1`, and `New.stdLattice.semichar x` is `selfDualAddChar E (c₀ / 2 * x* x)`.

modules.title: Hyperbolic space and splittings of a hermitian space along isotropic subspaces
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Mixed Schrödinger models, zero terms and named data
modules.note:
A hermitian space `V : New.Space E n s` has Gram matrix `V.J` over `E` and an adelic frame `V.x`
taking it to `New.stdForm E s`. `New.G E s` is the adelic unitary group of that form, and `V.Γ` is
its group of rational points. Here `E` is a CM field (`CMType E`), and `WeilData E` supplies the
purely imaginary `j` (`star j = -j`) used below. The file constructs hyperbolic space together with
its frame, and defines adelic matrices that are orthonormal at the infinite places and integral at
the finite ones. It then studies a splitting, or Witt decomposition,
`V = (range l ⊕ range k) ⊥ i V₀` with `l` and `k` isotropic and dual: it gives the frames and
coordinates of the splitting in adelic form, the Levi and unipotent elements of the stabiliser of
`range k`, the law of a mixed model, and points adapted to the splitting.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.hyperbolicSpace`: the hyperbolic space of rank `2 p` as a `New.Space`, that is, with an
  adelic frame that carries its Gram matrix to the standard form of signs `New.hyperbolicSigns p`
  (`p` times `+1`, `p` times `-1`).
* `New.Exchange.IsOrthoIntegral`: adelic matrices with orthonormal columns at the infinite places
  and integral finite part. The frame of `New.hyperbolicSpace` and its inverse are such
  (`New.Exchange.isOrthoIntegral_hyperbolicSpace`), and the property is stable under products, block
  sums and choice of columns.
* `New.Space.Splitting.levi`, `New.Space.Splitting.radicalElement`: Levi and unipotent elements;
  every `g` with `g k = k a` is a product of the two
  (`New.Space.Splitting.exists_eq_radicalElement_mul_levi`), and the unipotent elements make up the
  unipotent radical (`New.Space.Splitting.exists_eq_radicalElement_iff`).
* `New.Space.Splitting.IsAdapted`: elements of `G` adapted to a splitting and to `t` in `GL_p(𝔸)`;
  they exist (`New.Space.Splitting.exists_isAdapted_and_frame_eq`).
* `New.Space.Splitting.siegelParabolic_sup_symm_eq_top`: if `V₀` is zero, the stabilizers of the
  spans of `k` and of `l` generate the rational unitary group of `V`.
* `New.Space.Splitting.exists_isCompact_rat_mul_radicalElement_mem`: the rational points of the
  unipotent radical are cocompact.

Notions from other files:
* `New.stdForm E s`: the diagonal adelic matrix that is `diag s` at every infinite place and the
  identity at the finite places.
* `New.G.adeleMatrix`: the `n × n` adelic matrix of an element of the adelic unitary group
  `New.G E s`.
* `New.evalInf w`: evaluation of an adele at the infinite place `w`, a ring map to `ℂ`.
* `Ô E`: the integral finite adeles.

modules.title: Data named by Schwartz–Bruhat functions: Heisenberg laws, transport, Weil action
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Mixed Schrödinger models, zero terms and named data
modules.note:
Let S be a set of finite places disjoint from its conjugate S̄. A Schwartz–Bruhat function Ψ above S
names an operator `V.schrodingerOp S Ψ` on 𝒮(V). The box function names the projection P^S =
`New.Space.projOn` S. Its translates name Heisenberg translates ϱ(αy₊) P^S of it, with α the finite
idele of `New.WeilData`. Naming is compatible with products of data. For general g, Ψ is composed
with g_f⁻¹ and the vector also changes.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.schrodingerOp`: sends ∑ c_y (translate of the indicator by y) to the operator ∑ c_y
  ϱ(αy₊) P^S, with y₊ the part of y above S ∪ S̄ and P^S = `New.Space.projOn` S.
* `New.Space.rho_schrodingerOp`: naming is equivariant for the Heisenberg operators of the parts of
  vectors above S ∪ S̄.
* `New.Space.dataInner_schrodingerOp`: the inner product of two named vectors factors.
* `New.Space.schrodingerOp_union`: for disjoint `S`, `T` with `S ∪ T` disjoint from its conjugate, a
  product of functions names the composite.
* `New.Space.omega_schrodingerOp`: for any `g`, `ω g (schrodingerOp Ψ f) = schrodingerOp (Ψ ∘ g_f⁻¹)
  u`, where `u` is `ω g` applied to the name of the box function composed with `g_f`, and `u` is
  fixed by `V.projOn S`.
* `New.Space.omega_schrodingerOp_of_mem_supportedOn`: `g` supported on `S ∪ S̄` acts by
  `Ψ ↦ Ψ ∘ g⁻¹`, times the conjugate of `New.chiAdelic` at the `S`-part of `det g`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with
  xᴴJx equal to the diagonal matrix of its signs at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.Space.ϱ`: the Heisenberg operator of an adelic vector `y` on `𝒮 V`.

modules.title: Real data, the entire theta function, and the real vacuum in the mixed model
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Mixed Schrödinger models, zero terms and named data
modules.note:
A datum f in `New.𝒮` V is a function on adelic vectors, f(x) = θ(ϱ(x)f), where θ is the theta
functional and ϱ the Heisenberg operators. For v in Fock space we write v ⊗ f = ∫ v(y) ϱ(y) f dy
over real vectors y, and compute its inner products and theta value. If all signs are +1 and f is
fixed by the real vacuum projection, then the theta function Θ_f(y) = f(y) exp(|y|²/2) is entire.
The last part computes the real vacuum and the map `T 0` in a mixed Schrödinger model `T`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.eq_zero_of_apply_realVec_eq_zero`: f is determined by its values on real vectors, by
  strong approximation and quasi-periodicity under rational vectors.
* `New.Space.entireTheta`: the function Θ_f(y) = f(y) exp(|y|²/2).
* `New.Space.entireTheta_eq_integral`, `New.Space.differentiable_entireTheta`: if all signs are +1
  and inserting the Gaussian as real vector (`New.Space.projReal`) fixes f, then Θ_f is an integral
  against the kernel exp(∑ y_p conj w_p), hence entire.
* `New.Space.theta_integrated_polyVector_eq_integral_entireTheta`: if all signs are +1, the theta
  value of v_P ⊗ f for a polynomial vector v_P is ∫ P(conj y) Θ_f(y) exp(−|y|²) dy.
* `New.Space.Splitting.IsAdapted.omega_projReal_of_isMixedLaw`: in a mixed Schrödinger model `T`,
  the value `T x (ω(g) P f)` is a Gaussian in the real point `x`, for `P` the real vacuum projection
  and `g` adapted to the splitting.
* `New.Space.Splitting.IsAdapted.exists_apply_zero_omega_integrated_eq`: `T 0 ∘ ω(g)` acts on the
  real part by a bounded map of Fock spaces. Here `V.integrated v f`, written v ⊗ f, gives `f` the
  real part `v`, and `V.projReal` is the case of the real vacuum.

modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts

modules.note:
This file works with a splitting (Witt decomposition) `D` of `V = (range l ⊕ range k) ⊥ ι V₀`.
A vector `f` of `𝒮 V` is applied to an adelic vector `x` through its theta function:
`f x = θ (ϱ(x) f)` (`New.Space.theta_rho`). The file defines the zero term ev = `D.zeroTerm` :
𝒮 V → 𝒮 V₀ and the slices f[x] = `D.slice x f` = ev(ϱ(l x) f), and proves that the slices obey
the mixed law. It shows that zero terms can be taken in stages and that the zero term depends only
on `ι` and the span of `k`. It studies families obeying the mixed law at adapted points, bounds
sums of slices over rational points and writes θ_V as the sum of θ_{V₀} over the slices.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.Splitting.zeroTerm`: the zero term `𝒮 V → 𝒮 V₀`, the mean of `f (ι y + k b)` over
  `b ∈ 𝔸^p / E^p`; `New.Space.Splitting.slice x` is `D.zeroTerm ∘L V.ϱ (D.lAdelic *ᵥ x)`.
* `New.Space.Splitting.tsum_enorm_slice_le`, `New.Space.Splitting.hasSum_theta_slice`:
  over the rational points `ξ`, `∑_ξ ‖f[ξ]‖ ≤ M ‖f‖` and `θ_V f = ∑_ξ θ_{V₀} (f[ξ])`.
* `New.Space.Splitting.IsAdapted.slice_omega_vacElem`: for `g` adapted to `t`, the slices of
  ω(g) vac are a nonzero constant times `‖vacuumFn (tᴴ x)‖ ^ 2` times the vacuum of `V₀`. The case
  of any `g` when `V₀` is zero needs the Iwasawa decomposition and is
  `New.Space.Splitting.exists_slice_omega_vacElem_of_isEmpty`, in
  `Lib.SiegelWeil.Formula.LagrangianZeroTerms`.

modules.note:
This file proves that the slice map x ↦ f[x] = `D.slice x f` of a splitting `D` is continuous and
integrable on `𝔸^p`. Take `g` with `g k = k a`, `a ∈ GL_p(𝔸)`, acting as `g₀` on `V₀`. Then ev
ω(g) = χ_𝔸(det a)⁻¹ ω(g₀) ev, where ev is the zero term and χ_𝔸 = `New.chiAdelic`. The file then
proves that θ is invariant under the rational unitary group. When `V₀` is zero, the function
x ↦ f[x] plays the part of a vector of the Schrödinger model on `𝔸^p`; this identification is not
stated here, and the space L²(𝔸^p) is not used.

  comes from `New.Space.Splitting.exists_hyperbolic_levi_multiplier_nonneg`.

modules.literature:
Known result: Schrödinger and mixed models of the Weil representation and the action of parabolic
subgroups. Here the groups are adelic unitary groups of spaces `New.Space` over a CM field with
`New.WeilData`, and the vectors have integrable coefficients instead of being Schwartz functions.
The representation is normalised by its vacuum coefficient, so the formulas for the parabolic
subgroup are proved rather than taken as the definition. Source: C. Mœglin, M.-F. Vignéras, J.-L.
Waldspurger, Correspondances de Howe sur un corps p-adique, LNM 1291, 1987; S. Kudla, Splitting
metaplectic covers of dual reductive pairs, Israel J. Math. 87 (1994) 361–401; A. Weil, Acta Math.
111 (1964) n° 16–19, 41.

Known result: Adelic Weil representation of a unitary group and the invariant theta functional. Here
the CM fields have enough roots of unity and carry a splitting character and a self-dual rank-one
lattice, and the Weil representation is built without a polarisation. Vectors are integrable
coefficients against a vacuum, the splitting is fixed by the vacuum coefficient, and the sign of the
finite cocycle comes from a congruence modulo 4. Source: A. Weil, Sur certains groupes d'opérateurs
unitaires, Acta Math. 111 (1964), n° 16-19 Thm 4, n° 41 Thm 6; S. Kudla, Splitting metaplectic
covers of dual reductive pairs, Israel J. Math. 87 (1994) 361-401; H. Reiter, Metaplectic Groups and
Segal Algebras, LNM 1382 (1989) (space of data, after H. Feichtinger, On a new Segal algebra,
Monatsh. Math. 92 (1981)); E. Zelenov, p-adic Heisenberg group and Maslov index, Comm. Math. Phys.
155 (1993) 489-502, Prop. 4 (cocycle of three lattices); Robinson and Rawnsley, Mem. AMS 410 (1989)
(real normalisation).

modules.title: Adapted splittings: hyperbolic polarisation, Hom spaces, composition and stages
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Mixed Schrödinger models, zero terms and named data
modules.note:
A splitting `D : V'.Splitting V p` (`New.Space.Splitting`) writes a hermitian space `V'` as `V` plus
`p` hyperbolic planes, by dual isotropic frames `D.l`, `D.k` and an isometry `D.i`. An adelic matrix
is `New.Exchange.IsOrthoIntegral` if it has orthonormal columns at the infinite places and integral
finite part. The splitting `D` is adapted, `New.Exchange.IsBaseAdapted D`, if its adelic frame
`(l, k, i)` has this property.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.hyperbolicSplitting`: the hyperbolic space `New.hyperbolicSpace E p` splits
  (`New.Space.Splitting`) over the zero space `New.stdSpace E Empty`. Here `l` is the first `p`
  basis vectors and `k` is the last `p` basis vectors.
* `New.Exchange.removePlanes`: the tautological splitting over V of the sum
  `New.Exchange.hyperbolicSum` of hyperbolic planes and V. An instance shows that the tautological
  splitting is adapted.
* `New.Exchange.adaptedHomBasis`: the change of basis `(x⁻¹)ᴴ ⊗ 1` given by the adelic frame `x` of
  `T`.
* `New.Exchange.homSlice_eq_adapted_slice`: the term `A.homSlice T x` is a mixed term of
  `A.homSource T`, after the change of basis `adaptedHomBasis p T`.
* `New.Exchange.isAdapted_homSource`: if `A` is adapted, `A.homSource T` is adapted in the basis
  `adaptedHomBasis p T`.
* `New.Exchange.exists_isBaseAdapted_reindex`,
  `New.Exchange.exists_isBaseAdapted_comp_removePlanes`: an adapted splitting with a single plane
  (`e : Unit ≃ p`) can be reindexed by `Unit`. An adapted splitting can be factored through `V` plus
  some of the planes.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to the diagonal matrix of its signs at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.Space.Splitting.IsAdapted`: `D.IsAdapted g t` says that the matrix g⁻¹(l tᴴ⁻¹, k t, ι) of
  adelic frames (`frameAt`) is `IsOrthoIntegral`.
* `New.Space.Splitting.homSource`: From a splitting (k, l, ι) of V over V₀, the splitting of
  Hom(V,T) over Hom(V₀,T) with frames J_T⁻¹⊗(kᴴJ)ᵀ, 1⊗(lᴴJ)ᵀ, 1⊗(J₀⁻¹ιᴴJ)ᵀ.
* `New.Space.Splitting.comp`: From splittings of V over V₀ (rank p) and V₀ over V₁ (rank q), the
  splitting of V over V₁ with frames (k, ik'), (l, il') and embedding ii'.
* `New.Space.Splitting.kCoord`, `lCoord`: the adelic matrices lᴴε, kᴴε (ε = `stdForm`), which send
  la + ιw + kb to b and to a; `iCoord`, built from ιᴴε and the signs, sends it to w.
* `New.Space.Splitting.homSlice`: `A.homSlice T x` is the zero term of `A.homSource T` after the
  Heisenberg operator of the map `x * A.kCoord` in `Hom(W', T)`.

modules.title: Real, named and finite slices of data in the mixed model of an adapted splitting
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Mixed Schrödinger models, zero terms and named data
modules.note:
For a splitting `D` of `V` over `V₀` adapted at the point 1 in a basis `t` (`D.IsAdapted 1 t`), the
adelic mixed model separates into a real part and a finite part. Vectors named by a function `Φ` of
their components at finitely many finite places have slices that are scalar multiples of named
vectors when `Φ` factors in an adapted frame. For `Φ` standard in an integral frame, orthogonality
of characters then gives the source term explicitly.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.Splitting.IsAdapted.mixedModel`: the mixed Schrödinger–Fock model v ↦ v[a]
  (`New.Fock.MixedModel`) at the infinite places that D induces.
* `New.Exchange.zeroTerm_integrated`: the zero term of v ⊗ f is v[0] ⊗ (zero term of f°).
* `New.Exchange.slice_integrated`: the slice at `(t⁻¹)ᴴ x` of v ⊗ f is the real slice of v at
  the real part of x tensored with the slice of f° at the finite part.
* `New.Exchange.ReadsAt.lift`: a chosen continuous additive section of the map `π` that reads the
  components at `S`.
* `New.Exchange.slice_localDatum`: if `Φ` factors in an adapted frame, a slice is a scalar times
  a named vector.
* `New.Exchange.adaptedFrame`: a base-adapted splitting gives, through `π`, an integral frame over
  `F` in three blocks.
* `New.Exchange.ReadsAt.homSlice_localDatum`: the source term of `v ⊗ Φ` for `Φ` that is standard
  in that frame at the matrices whose first block is `π` of the finite part of the given point.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space.Splitting`: A decomposition V = (lE^p ⊕ kE^p) ⊥ ιV₀ over E: isotropic frames l, k with
  l*Jk = 1 for the hermitian form J of V, an isometry ι from V₀ orthogonal to both, and
  rk V = rk V₀ + 2p.
* `New.Space.Splitting.IsAdapted`: `D.IsAdapted g t` says that the matrix g⁻¹(l tᴴ⁻¹, k t, ι) of
  adelic frames has orthonormal columns at the infinite places and integral finite part.
* `New.𝔸`: The product of one copy of ℂ for each infinite place of E with the finite adeles 𝔸_f:
  the adele ring of E when E is totally complex.
* `New.Space.Splitting.slice`: the slice `f ↦ f[x]` at `x ∈ 𝔸^p`, a bounded map from 𝒮(V) to
  𝒮(V₀).
* `New.Exchange.IsBaseAdapted`: The adelic frame (l, k, ι) of the splitting has orthonormal columns
  at every infinite place and integral entries at every finite place.
* `New.Exchange.IntegralFrame`: An integral invertible matrix cut into column blocks (K I L), with
  its integral inverse cut into row blocks K′, I′, L′. `adaptedFrame h D` is the frame (k, ι, l) of
  an adapted splitting read through π.

modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts

modules.note:
The hermitian space `W'` splits as an isotropic line, `W` and a dual line (the splitting
`A : W'.Splitting W Unit`), and `V'` splits as an isotropic line `B`, `V` and a dual line (the
splitting `X : V'.Splitting V Unit`). This file studies the zero term along `Hom(W, B)` of slices of
vectors in the mixed models of the Weil representation at the real places.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Exchange.realTargetZeroTerm W X`: the zero term along `Hom(W, B)` at the real places.
* `New.Exchange.lineTermReal_true_eq_realTargetZeroTerm`: the real part of the line term is this
  zero term of a slice.
* `New.Exchange.exists_realTargetZeroTerm_eq`: every Schwartz vector is such a zero term.
* `New.Exchange.realSlice_realPairWeil`, `New.Exchange.exists_realTargetZeroTerm_realPairWeil`: real
  points of the target group act on slices, and those with `lineVector X` as an eigenvector at every
  place act on zero terms when `2 ∣ card n`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space.Splitting V' V p`: a decomposition of `V'` into isotropic frames `l`, `k` with `p`
  columns and an isometric copy of `V`; `kAdelic`, `lAdelic`, `iAdelic` are its adelic frames, and
  `IsBaseAdapted` says that together they are orthonormal at the infinite places and integral at the
  finite places.
* `homSource`, `homTarget`: the splittings of `Hom(W', V')` over `Hom(W, V')` and of `Hom(W, V')`
  over `Hom(W, V)` induced by `A` and by `X`; `zeroTerm` is the zero term of a splitting.
* `IsAdapted.mixedModel`: the mixed model at the real places of a splitting adapted to a basis; its
  `slice` at a point, and `realSlice` for the splitting `homSource`, map the Fock space `PairFock`
  of one space of homomorphisms to that of a smaller one.
* `lineTerm`, `lineTermReal`: the operator that translates along the line and takes both zero terms,
  and its real part; `realPairWeil γ γ'` is the real Weil action of a pair with weights.

modules.title: Graded hermitian spaces X ⊕ J_s, Bessel subgroups, the map T, and c_λ in a frame
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Bessel periods and unfolding of theta integrals
modules.note:
A hermitian space `V = X ⊕ J_s` is presented (`New.Grading`) as a space `X` with an orthonormal
basis plus a string of `s` vectors with antidiagonal Gram matrix, whose entries are 1 except `-N`
for the middle vector (`N = N̄ ≠ 0`). The weight, also called grade, is `0` on `X` and `s - 1 - 2i`
on the `i`-th string vector. The grading defines three objects in `U(V)(𝔸)`: the unipotent subgroup
`New.Grading.unipotent`, which raises weights; the embedding `New.Grading.inclX` of `U(X)`; and the
Bessel subgroup `New.Grading.besselGroup`. These are described by matrix entries in rational
coordinates. For a second graded space `V' = X' ⊕ J_(s-1)` the map `T : V → V'`
(`New.Grading.stringMap`) is studied, and separately the matrix coefficient c_λ of a discrete series
is transported to `U(J)` through a frame.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Grading`: a presentation of `V` in this form, with a constant `genericConst` for the generic
  character.
* `New.Grading.stringMap`: the map between two graded spaces that kills `X` and sends each string
  vector to a multiple of the string vector with the same number (to `0` if there is none). It has
  degree at least `-1` when `s' = s - 1`. `New.Grading.AgreesWithStringMap` is partial agreement
  with it.
* `New.Grading.besselProj`, `New.Grading.exists_besselGroup_proj`,
  `New.Grading.exists_unipotent_mul_inclX`: taking the X-block is a homomorphism from
  `New.Grading.besselGroup` onto U(X) with kernel `New.Grading.unipotent`, split by
  `New.Grading.inclX`.
* `New.isIdempotentKernel_dsCoeffInFrame`: for λ with a large gap, the formal degree times
  `New.HCParam.dsCoeffInFrame l` is an idempotent kernel on `U J` (Schur orthogonality).
* `New.Grading.hasDegreeGe_zero_mul_stringMap_mul_sub`: the Bessel subgroups
  `New.Grading.besselGroup` of both spaces fix `T` modulo degree at least `0`.
* `New.Grading.formAdjoint_stringMap_mul_stringMap_eq_shift`,
  `New.Grading.stringMap_mul_formAdjoint_stringMap_eq_shift`: `T† T` is the shift
  `New.Grading.shift` of `V`, and `T T†` is that of `V'` when the two constants agree;
  `New.Grading.formAdjoint_stringMap_mul_stringMap` states both.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point: a matrix J over E and an x in GL_n(𝔸) such that xᴴJx
  is diag(ε) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places. `V.Γ` is the group of g whose matrix
  in rational coordinates has entries in E; `New.stdSpace E X` is the definite space on X with point
  1.
* `New.𝔸`: the adele ring of the CM field E, as the product of ℂ^f (one copy of ℂ for each infinite
  place) and the finite adeles.
* `New.G`: the adelic unitary group G = G_∞ × G_f of the form diag(ε) at the infinite places and 1
  at the finite places; `g.adeleMatrix` is the adelic matrix of g.
* `New.IsHermitianInvolution J`: the complex matrix J satisfies J* = J and J² = 1.
* `New.HCParam.HasLargeGap`, `New.HCParam.formalDegree`: for l = 2λ and signs ε on n indices, the
  condition that λ has gap 500n³+A for a natural number A, and the reciprocal of the integral of
  |c_λ|² over U(diag ε) for the compact dual measure.

modules.title: The lattice of a finite point of a graded space
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Bessel periods and unfolding of theta integrals
modules.note:
A finite point `x` of the unitary group of a hermitian space `V` gives a self-dual lattice
`New.Space.lattice` over `Ô`, spanned by the orthonormal frame `V.xFin * x`. A grading
(`New.Grading`) writes `V = X ⊕ X^⊥`, where `X^⊥` is spanned by the string. The lattice has an
intersection `Λ'⁻` with `X^⊥` (`New.Grading.latticeMinus`) and a projection `Λ'⁺` to `X^⊥`
(`New.Grading.latticePlus`); `Λ⁻` is the intersection for the point `1`.

* `New.Space.mem_lattice_iff_formFin`: the lattice of a point is self-dual.
* `New.Space.lattice_eq_iff`: two points have the same lattice if and only if they differ by an
  integral unitary matrix.
* `New.Grading.mem_latticeMinus_iff_formFin`, `New.Grading.mem_latticePlus_iff_formFin`: the
  intersection and the projection are dual to each other.
* `New.Grading.exists_lattice_inclXFin_mul_eq`: lattices of points with the same intersection with
  `X^⊥` are conjugate under the unitary group of `X`, assuming `[HasPrimitiveRoot5040 E]`.

modules.title: Integrals over the Bessel subgroup and the orbits surviving unipotent twists
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Bessel periods and unfolding of theta integrals
modules.note:
A hermitian space `V` is graded by `Y`, which presents it as `X` plus a string of `s` vectors, and
`B` is its Bessel (Fourier–Jacobi) subgroup. For a second space `V'` graded by `Y'` with a string of
length `s - 1`, the file determines which terms of a Fourier expansion over rational maps
`w : V → V'` survive the unipotent twists. Each such `w` can be moved to a map of type
`New.Grading.AgreesWithStringMap`, and if that map also survives with degrees `Y'.gradeOf`, then
that map minus `Y.stringMap Y'` has degree `≥ 0`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Grading.isCocompact_ratBessel`: the adelic group `B` is compact modulo its rational points.
* `New.Grading.besselMeasure`: the measure that integrates over `B` modulo its rational points.
* `New.Grading.integral_besselMeasure_eq_of_mean`: such an integral is a fixed multiple of an
  integral over `U(X)` modulo its rational points, after averaging over the row of the unipotent
  part.
* `New.Grading.Survives`: no unipotent twist kills the term at `w`.
* `New.Grading.exists_agreesWithStringMap`: a rational `w` that is not killed can be moved by a
  rational unitary element of `V'` to a map of type `New.Grading.AgreesWithStringMap`;
  `New.Grading.agreesWithStringMap_mul_iff`: that element is unique up to `Y'.besselGroup`.
* `New.Grading.hasDegreeGe_of_survives`: a map of type `New.Grading.AgreesWithStringMap` is killed
  unless `w - Y.stringMap Y'` has degree `≥ 0`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to the diagonal matrix of its signs at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.eichlerMap`: `eichlerMap J x u ς` is v ↦ v + h(u, v)x − h(x, v)(u + ςx), h the form of J.
* `New.Space.homBicharacter`: the phase `ψ ((j / 2) tr (y† x))` of two adelic maps `x`, `y`.

modules.title: The character `ψ_U` and the function `𝒲_φ`
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Bessel periods and unfolding of theta integrals
modules.note:
Let `Y` be a grading of the hermitian space `V` (`New.Grading`): a splitting of its basis into a
set `X` and a string of `s` vectors. It gives the Bessel group `R = U ⋊ H`
(`New.Grading.besselGroup`). Here `U` (`New.Grading.unipotent`) is the group of points whose matrix
in rational coordinates, minus `1`, raises grades, and `H` is the unitary group of the standard
definite space on `X`, embedded by `New.Grading.inclX`. Write `U^{≥2}` for the points whose matrix
minus `1` raises grades by at least `2`.

This file defines the projection `R → H` (`New.Grading.leviPart`) and the function
`ψ_U (u) = ψ (½ ȷ tr (𝔢 u))` (`New.Grading.unipotentChar`). It shows that `ψ_U` is a character on
`U^{≥2}(𝔸)`, trivial on rational points and invariant under conjugation by `H(𝔸)`. It defines
`ψ_U`-equivariant functions on `[R]` (`New.Grading.IsEquivariant`) and the function `𝒲_φ`
(`New.Grading.sourceFn`) of an algebraic form `φ`. It shows that `𝒲_φ` is `ψ_U`-equivariant when `s`
is odd, since then `U = U^{≥2}`, and that it is the only such function with its values on `H`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Grading.gradeOf`: the grade of a basis index, `0` on `X` and `s - 1 - 2 i` on the string
  vector `i`.
* `New.HasDegreeGe w' w d x`: the matrix `x` raises grades by at least `d`, that is `x b a = 0`
  whenever `w' b < w a + d`.
* `New.Grading.shift`: the rational endomorphism `𝔢` of `V` that sends each string vector to a
  multiple of the next one and kills `X` and the last string vector.
* `New.algFormCoeff 1 t φ`: the function `h ↦ t (conjWeylRep κ e h_∞⁻¹ (φ h_fin))` on `H(𝔸)` of an
  algebraic form `φ` and a linear functional `t` on its values.

modules.title: Constant terms of Weil functions along maps of positive degree
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Bessel periods and unfolding of theta integrals
modules.note:
This file studies the theta kernel on `Hom(V, V')` for gradings `Y` of `V` and `Y'` of `V'`
(`New.Grading`), with strings of lengths `s` and `s'`. It computes how the Weil action moves
Heisenberg operators and zero terms. It defines the constant term `New.Grading.constTerm` of
`f ∈ 𝒮 (Hom (V, V'))` along the maps of positive degree. It proves the transformation laws of this
constant term and the Fourier expansion of `f 0` in constant terms. It defines the unfolded
function `New.Grading.unfoldStep` and, for `s' = s - 1`, proves its continuity and invariance
properties.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Seesaw.pairWeil_homHeisenbergOp`: the Weil action of a pair `(g, g₀)` moves the Heisenberg
  operator of `w` to that of `g₀ w g⁻¹`, in rational coordinates.
* `New.Grading.constTerm`: the constant term of `f ∈ 𝒮 (Hom (V, V'))` along the maps of positive
  degree; `New.Grading.constTerm_eq_theta_zeroTerm` and `New.Grading.exists_splitting_constTerm`
  write it as a theta value in a mixed model.
* `New.Grading.constTerm_mul_of_mem_ratBessel`, `New.Grading.constTerm_mul_of_mem_unipotent` (both
  cases together: `New.Grading.constTerm_mul`), `New.Grading.constTerm_congr_rat`,
  `New.Grading.constTerm_eq_homBicharacter_mul`: its transformation laws.
* `New.Grading.hasSum_constTerm_out`, `New.Grading.exists_tsum_enorm_constTerm_le` (both together:
  `New.Grading.hasSum_constTerm`): Fourier expansion of `f 0` in constant terms, with a bound.
* `New.Grading.unfoldStep`: the unfolded function `𝒲'`. The laws of the constant term and the
  following properties are proved for `s' = s - 1`. `New.Grading.continuous_unfoldStep`: it is
  continuous if `W` is equivariant. `New.Grading.unfoldStep_rat_mul`: it is left invariant under the
  rational points of the Bessel subgroup of `Y'`. `New.Grading.isEquivariant_unfoldStep`: if `W` is
  equivariant and `Y'.genericConst = Y.genericConst`, each `γ ↦ 𝒲'(γ h)` is again equivariant
  (`New.Grading.IsEquivariant`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.𝒮`: The Banach space 𝒮(V) of integrable functions c on 𝔸^n with c(x) = ∫ c(y)β(y,x)e(x−y) dy,
  under the L¹ norm; β is the adelic bicharacter and e the vacuum function `New.vacuumFn`.
* `New.Grading.stringMap`, written `T`: the rational map `V → V'` that kills `X` and sends each

  there is none).
* `New.Grading.AgreesWithStringMap`: `w` agrees with `T` at the entries `(b, a)` where `a` has
  positive grade and `b` has grade below that of `a`.
* `New.Grading.ratBessel`: The rational points of U(V) that lie in the Bessel (Fourier–Jacobi)
  subgroup of the grading Y.

on `R(𝔸)` that is supported on one coset of a level in the finite variable, and depends there only
on the real variable, has an integral that reduces to `R(F_∞)`.

Notions used in the statements:
* `G E ε = GInf E ε × Gf E ι` is the adelic unitary group `G(𝔸) = G_∞ × G_f`.
* `Y.besselGroup` is the Bessel (Fourier–Jacobi) subgroup `R(𝔸)` of the grading
  `Y : Grading V N X s` of the space `V : Space E ι ε` over the CM field `E` (both defined in
  earlier files); its real points `R(F_∞)` are `Y.besselReal`, and its finite points `R(𝔸_fin)` are
  `Y.besselFin`.

modules.title: Vanishing theta descents for unitary groups: Fourier coefficients and periods
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Bessel periods and unfolding of theta integrals
modules.note:
This file defines the predicate `New.SiegelWeil.DescentsVanish`, the vanishing of all theta descents
of a function on `U(V)(𝔸)` to `U(W)(𝔸)` for data that are vacua above given places. It studies the
Fourier coefficients of theta lifts between unitary groups along the centre of the unipotent
radical. These coefficients are written as sums over rational frames. Then, for an invertible Gram
matrix, Witt's theorem writes them as integrals modulo a stabiliser.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.SiegelWeil.DescentsVanish`: the descents of `Y` vanish for all data that are vacua above the
  places of `S`.
* `New.Space.Splitting.centreCoeff_integral_eq_tsum`: the coefficient at `j β` keeps the frames `x`
  with Gram matrix `β`.
* `New.SiegelWeil.integral_blockEmb_eq_zero_of_descentsVanish`: split `V = V″ ⊕ V°` into blocks of
  ranks `n₁` and `n₂`. Let `o₁` be the frame of `V″` and `I(h)` the period over `[U(V°)]` of the
  right translate by `h`. The vanishing of a Fourier coefficient of the descents makes `I`, times a
  weight, orthogonal to every additive character of the frame `h⁻¹ o₁` that ignores its components
  at the places of `T` and their conjugates, hence, by Stone–Weierstrass, to every continuous
  function of these characters. On the support of the weight `I` is such a function, so it vanishes
  there.

Notions from other files:
* `New.𝒮`: the Banach space of data on which the Weil representation of a hermitian space acts;
  `New.Space.projOn` projects it on the vectors that are vacua above a set of finite places and
  their conjugates.
* `New.pairTheta W V a b f`: the theta kernel on `U(W)(𝔸) × U(V)(𝔸)` of a datum `f` on `Hom(W, V)`,
  twisted by the characters `a`, `b` of `U(1)`. `New.pairThetaKer` bundles it, and `New.Space.lift`
  for `(pairThetaKer W V a b).swap` integrates a function on `U(V)(𝔸)` against it.
* `New.Space.Splitting.radicalCentre`: the parametrisation of the centre of the unipotent radical by
  adelic `p × p` matrices; `centreCoeff T F g` is the mean of `ψ (tr (T M)) * F (z M * g)` over the
  `M` modulo rational matrices, `z` being this parametrisation.
* `New.WeilData.upsilonU1`: the restriction of the splitting character υ to the norm-one ideles.
modules.literature:
Known result: Fourier coefficients of theta lifts as periods over stabilisers. Here a single
non-degenerate coefficient of a theta lift to a split unitary group is unfolded once by Witt's
theorem. Hence a form on the definite U(n) orthogonal to the theta kernels of the split space has
zero period over the complementary unitary group. Source: P. Walls, The theta correspondence,
periods of automorphic forms and special values of standard automorphic L-functions, arXiv
1501.01565 (2015), Prop. 2.1.1; S. Rallis, On the Howe duality conjecture, Compositio Math. 51
(1984) 333–399.

modules.title: One step of the seesaw unfolding of the theta integral over the Bessel group
modules.folder: Weil: The Weil representation and theta lifts
modules.group: Bessel periods and unfolding of theta integrals
modules.note:
This file unfolds the period of an equivariant function `W` (`New.Grading.IsEquivariant`) on the
Bessel group `New.Grading.besselGroup` of `Y` against the theta kernel, where the strings of `Y`
and `Y'` have lengths `s` and `s - 1`. The theta kernel at `(r, h)` is `θ` of the translate
`twistedPairWeil α (r, h) Φ`; it is expanded in constant terms indexed by rational maps `V → V'`
modulo those of degree at least zero (`New.Grading.nonnegMaps`). Over a set of classes that is
stable under the rational points of the Bessel group and in which no chosen representative survives
(`New.Grading.Survives`), the sum of the terms integrates to zero. Hence only the translates of
`𝒞 = New.Grading.agreeingClasses` by the rational points of `U(V')` contribute. This writes the
period as a sum of values of `New.Grading.unfoldStep`, and its integral against a rapidly decreasing
automorphic `y` as an integral of `New.Grading.unfoldStep` times `y`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Grading.hasSum_unfoldStep`: for `W` equivariant, the period of `W` against the theta kernel
  at `h` is the sum of the values of `New.Grading.unfoldStep` at `γ h` over the rational points `γ`
  of `U(V')`, modulo those of `Y'.besselGroup` on the left.
* `New.Grading.integral_besselGroup_unfold`: the period of `W` against the theta integral of a
  rapidly decreasing automorphic `y` unfolds to the integral of `New.Grading.unfoldStep` times `y`
  modulo the rational points of `Y'.besselGroup`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.𝒮`: The Banach space 𝒮(V) of integrable functions c on 𝔸^n with c(x) = ∫ c(y)β(y,x)e(x−y) dy,
  under the L¹ norm; β is the adelic bicharacter and e the vacuum function `New.vacuumFn`.
* `New.Grading.ratBessel`: The rational points of U(V) that lie in the Bessel (Fourier–Jacobi)
  subgroup of the grading Y.
* `New.Grading.constTerm`: the constant term of `f` at `w` along the maps of positive degree.
* `New.Grading.unfoldStep`: the function `h ↦ ∫ W(r) * Y.constTermAtStringMap Y' α f r h dr` on
  U(V′)(𝔸), integrated over the Bessel group of `Y` modulo its rational points.
* `New.Grading.agreeingClasses`: the set `𝒞` of classes whose chosen representative agrees with
  `T = Y.stringMap Y'` (`New.Grading.AgreesWithStringMap`).
modules.literature:
Transfer of Bessel and Fourier–Jacobi periods under a theta lift (one unfolding step).
Here the setting is unitary pairs and hook orbits with a definite complement, and the Bessel and
Fourier–Jacobi cases are treated together. The period is taken against any continuous automorphic
function with the generic unipotent character, for a rapidly decreasing form, and the unfolded
integral converges absolutely. Source: B. Wang Peng Jun, Global theta lifting and automorphic
periods associated to nilpotent orbits, J. Number Theory 271 (2025) 122–149, Prop. 3.2 and Thm. 4.5;
for the local case, R. Gomez, C.-B. Zhu, GAFA 24 (2014) 796–853; for unitary hooks, M. Furusawa, K.
Morimoto, Math. Ann. 391 (2025) §3.
